Both numbers have three digits. Multiply only their last digits, 7 and 6, to see what the product must end in. Then think how many digits the product of two 3-digit numbers can have.

Here is a similar one. The product of star, 3 and star, 4 must end in 2, because 3 times 4 equals 12. Two 2-digit numbers give a product from 10 times 10, which is 100, up to 99 times 99, which is 9801. So 1472 could be the product, but 1475 could not.
steps: Multiply the last digits. The product must end in 2. 7 times 6 equals 42.
Two 3-digit numbers multiply to at least 100 times 100, which is 10000, and to less than 1000 times 1000, which is 1000000. So the product has 5 or 6 digits.
1342 has too few digits, 9933012 has too many, and 51276 does not end in 2.
Only 312312 has the right size and ends in 2. For example, 507 times 616 equals 312312.

PYQ_2019_Q33.q: A boy celebrated his 10th birthday on 15th April 2019 which was a Monday. His 12th birthday will fall on which day of the week?
hints: The 12th birthday is two years after the 10th. Each ordinary year moves the day forward by 1, and a 29th February in between moves it by 2.
Go from 15th April 2019 to 15th April 2020 first. Check whether 29th February 2020 falls in between.

Similar example: a girl turns 8 on 10th May 2015, a Sunday. From May 2015 to May 2016 we pass 29th February 2016, so her 9th birthday is 2 days on, a Tuesday. The next year is ordinary, so her 10th birthday is a Wednesday.
steps: The 12th birthday is on 15th April 2021, two years later.
From April 2019 to April 2020 we pass 29th February 2020. So the day moves on by 2, from Monday to Wednesday.
From April 2020 to April 2021 there is no leap day. So the day moves on by 1, from Wednesday to Thursday.
The 12th birthday falls on a Thursday.

PYQ_2019_Q34.q: Given below are the measures of two angles of a triangle. Which one of them can be the measure of an isosceles triangle?
hints: An isosceles triangle has two equal angles. Use the fact that all three angles add up to 180 degrees to find the third angle of each pair.
For each pair, add the two angles and take the total from 180. See whether the third angle matches one of the two given.

Similar example: can 50 degrees and 80 degrees be two angles of an isosceles triangle? 50 plus 80 equals 130, and 180 minus 130 equals 50. The third angle is 50 degrees, the same as one already there, so yes.
steps: Try the pair 55 degrees and 70 degrees. Add them. 55 plus 70 equals 125.
Find the third angle. 180 minus 125 equals 55.
The angles are 55 degrees, 70 degrees and 55 degrees. Two are equal, so this triangle is isosceles.
The other pairs give third angles of 40 degrees, 60 degrees and 80 degrees, which match nothing in their pairs.
So the pair is 55 degrees and 70 degrees.

PYQ_2019_Q35.q: Ajay writes all the multiples of 4 up to 100 and Vijay writes all the multiples of 5 up to 100, in their notebooks. How many common numbers could you find in both their notebooks?
hints: A number in both notebooks is a multiple of 4 and also a multiple of 5. Such numbers are the common multiples of the two.
Find the smallest number that is a multiple of both 4 and 5. Every common number is a multiple of that one.
Example: multiples of 3 and multiples of 4 up to 50. The smallest common multiple is 12. The multiples of 12 up to 50 are 12, 24, 36 and 48, so there are 4 common numbers.
steps: A number in both notebooks must be a multiple of 4 and of 5. The smallest such number is 20.
Every common number is a multiple of 20. Up to 100 these are 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100.
Counting them, or working out 100 divided by 20, gives 5. There are 5 common numbers in both notebooks.

PYQ_2019_Q36.q: The side of a square is 4 x minus 3 y centimetres. Which of the following expression can represent the perimeter of this square?
hints: This is a perimeter question. Think about how many sides a square has and what is special about them.
A square has 4 equal sides. Multiply every part of the side 4 x minus 3 y, by 4.
Similar example: the side of a square is 2 A minus 5 b centimetres. The perimeter is 4 times the side. 4 times 2 A is 8 A and 4 times 5 b is 20 b, so the perimeter is 8 A minus 20 b centimetres.
steps: A square has 4 equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 times one side.
Multiply the x part by 4. 4 times 4 x is 16 x.
Multiply the y part by 4. 4 times 3 y is 12 y, and it is still being taken away.
So the perimeter is 16 x minus 12 y centimetres.

PYQ_2019_Q37.q: Express 7 kilograms 70 grams as a decimal.
hints: This is a weight conversion. The kilograms are the whole-number part, and the grams become the part after the decimal point once they are changed into kilograms.
There are 1000 grams in 1 kilogram, so divide the grams by 1000. Find 70 divided by 1000 first and watch where the digit 7 lands.
Here is a similar problem: write 9 kilograms 40 grams as a decimal. 40 grams is 40 divided by 1000, which is 0.04 kilograms. Adding the 9 kilograms gives 9 plus 0.04, which is 9.04 kilograms.
steps: There are 1000 grams in 1 kilogram, so 70 grams is 70 divided by 1000, which is 0.07 kilograms.
Add the whole kilograms: 7 plus 0.07 equals 7.07.
So 7 kilograms 70 grams, written as a decimal, is 7.07 kilograms.

PYQ_2019_Q38.q: Three and quarter dozen would be equal to how many articles?
hints: A dozen is a fixed number of things. Think of the amount in two parts: the whole dozens, and the quarter of a dozen.
Remember that one dozen is 12. Find how many are in 3 whole dozens, and then find a quarter of one dozen.
Here is a similar one: how many is two and a half dozen? Two dozen is 2 times 12, which is 24. Half a dozen is 12 divided by 2, which is 6. Together that is 24 plus 6, which is 30.
steps: One dozen is 12, so 3 dozen is 3 times 12, which is 36.
A quarter means one of 4 equal parts. A quarter of a dozen is 12 divided by 4, which is 3.
Add the two parts: 36 plus 3 equals 39. Three and a quarter dozen is 39 articles.

PYQ_2019_Q39.q: The H C F of 39 and 65 is:
hints: The H C F is the largest number that divides both numbers exactly. Breaking each number into a multiplication helps you see what they share.
Write 39 as a product of two smaller numbers. Then check whether either of those numbers divides 65.
Example: the H C F of 34 and 51. 34 equals 2 times 17 and 51 equals 3 times 17. Both contain 17 and share nothing else, so the H C F is 17.
steps: Break 39 into a multiplication: 39 equals 3 times 13.
Do the same for 65: 65 equals 5 times 13.
Both numbers contain 13, and 3 and 5 share nothing more. The H C F of 39 and 65 is 13.

PYQ_2019_Q40.q: When a boy asks a teacher, what is the time now, the teacher replies, the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of my watch makes an angle of 45 degrees now. What time is it now?
hints: This is about the angle between the hands of a clock. The 12 numbers split the clock into 12 equal gaps, and the hour hand keeps moving slowly between the numbers.

Each gap between two numbers on the clock is 360 divided by 12, which is 30 degrees. For each time, find where the minute hand points and where the hour hand has moved to, then count the gaps between them.

Similar example: at 3 30 the minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4. From there to 6 is 2 and a half gaps. Two gaps are 60 degrees and half a gap is 15 degrees, so the angle is 60 plus 15, which is 75 degrees.
steps: Each gap between two numbers on a clock is 30 degrees. 360 divided by 12 equals 30.
An angle of 45 degrees is 1 and a half gaps. 30 plus 15 equals 45.
At half past, the minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between two numbers. The trap is to forget that the hour hand has moved on.
At 7 30 the hour hand is halfway between 7 and 8. From 6 to 7 is one gap, and then there is half a gap more. That makes 45 degrees.
At 2 30 there are 3 and a half gaps and at 8 30 there are 2 and a half gaps, and at 1 15 the angle is a little more than 45 degrees. So the time is 7 30.

Q_CH01_001.q: The place value of 6 in 3,62,489 is:
hints: The place value of a digit is what it is worth because of where it sits. It is the digit multiplied by the value of its place.
Count the places in 3,62,489 from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands, lakhs. Find the place where the 6 sits.
Here is a similar one: in 7,25,318 the digit 5 is in the thousands place. Its place value is 5 times 1,000, which is 5,000.
steps: Count the places in 3,62,489 from the right: 9 is ones, 8 is tens, 4 is hundreds, 2 is thousands and 6 is ten-thousands.
Multiply the digit by the value of its place. 6 times 10000 equals 60000.
The place value of 6 is 60,000.

hints: The successor of a number is the number that comes just after it. This one needs care because every digit is a 9.
Add 1 to 99,999. Each 9 turns into 0 and passes 1 on to the next place, so think about how many digits the result will have.
Here is a similar one: the successor of 9,999 is 9,999 plus 1, which is 10,000. All the 9s become 0s and a new 1 appears in front.
steps: Successor means the next number, so add 1. 99999 plus 1 equals 100000.
Every 9 becomes 0 and a new 1 appears in front, so the result has six digits.
The successor of 99,999 is 1,00,000, which is one lakh.

hints: All start with 45. Compare the hundreds digit: 0, 3, 3, 2.
Two have 3 in the hundreds: 45,302 and 45,320. Compare the tens: 0 versus 2.
45,320 is greater than 45,302. Largest is 45,320.
steps: Compare digit by digit, from the left.
The largest is 45,320.

Q_CH01_004.q: What is C D X L I V in Hindu-Arabic numerals?
hints: To read a Roman numeral, look for a smaller symbol standing before a bigger one. That pair means subtract, and the pairs are then added together.
Split C D X L I V into three pairs: C D, X L and I V. Work out the value of each pair, remembering that the smaller symbol in front is taken away.
Here is a similar one: C M X C I X splits into C M, X C and I X. C M is 900, X C is 90 and I X is 9, so the number is 900 plus 90 plus 9, which is 999.
steps: C D is C before D, so take 100 away from 500. 500 minus 100 equals 400.
X L is X before L, so take 10 away from 50. 50 minus 10 equals 40.
I V is I before V, so take 1 away from 5. 5 minus 1 equals 4.
Add the three parts. C D X L I V is 444. 400 plus 40 plus 4 equals 444.

options: D C C L X X I X
D C C X C I X
D C C L X X X I X
D C C C I X
hints: 789 equals 700 plus 80 plus 9.
700 equals D C C, which is 500 plus 100 plus 100. 80 equals L X X X, which is 50 plus 10 plus 10 plus 10. 9 equals I X, which is 10 minus 1.
D C C L X X X I X
steps: 700 equals D C C.
80 equals L X X X.
9 equals I X.
789 equals D C C L X X X I X.

hints: Rounding to the nearest hundred means finding which hundred the number is closest to. The digit just to the right of the hundreds place decides.
4,567 lies between 4,500 and 4,600. Look at its tens digit: if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.
Here is a similar one: round 3,842 to the nearest hundred. It lies between 3,800 and 3,900. The tens digit is 4, which is less than 5, so it rounds down to 3,800.
steps: 4,567 lies between the hundreds 4,500 and 4,600.
The tens digit is 6. That is 5 or more, so the number is closer to the higher hundred and we round up.
4,567 rounded to the nearest hundred is 4,600.

Q_CH01_007.q: The number 5,43,21,678 has how many digits?
hints: Commas only help us read a big number. They are not digits. To find how many digits a number has, count every digit and skip the commas.
The commas split 5,43,21,678 into groups. Count the digits in each group and add the counts.
Here is a similar one: 2,45,301 has the groups 2, 45 and 301. That is 1 plus 2 plus 3, which is 6 digits.
steps: The commas split the number into the groups 5, 43, 21 and 678.
These groups have 1, 2, 2 and 3 digits. Add the counts. 1 plus 2 plus 2 plus 3 equals 8.
The number 5,43,21,678 has 8 digits.

hints: Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits. A digit of 0 adds nothing, so it can be left out.
Name the place of each digit in 30,507 from the left: ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, ones. Write the value of every digit that is not 0.
Here is a similar one: in 40,209 the 4 is worth 40,000, the 2 is worth 200 and the 9 is worth 9. The zeros add nothing, so 40,209 is 40,000 plus 200 plus 9.
steps: The 3 is in the ten-thousands place, so it is worth 30,000. The 0 in the thousands place adds nothing.
The 5 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 500. The 0 in the tens place adds nothing, and the 7 is worth 7.
So 30,507 in expanded form is 30,000 plus 500 plus 7.

hints: Ascending means smallest to largest. All start with 5, so compare the hundreds digit.
Hundreds: 2, 3, 4, 4. Then the tens, for the two with 4: 2 versus 3.
5,234 is less than 5,342, which is less than 5,423, which is less than 5,432.
steps: Compare hundreds: 2 is less than 3, which is less than 4.

hints: This sum has a subtraction, a multiplication and an addition all together. Think about which of the three has to be done first, before you go from left to right.
Work out 3 times 7 first and put that number in its place. Then do the subtraction and the addition in order from left to right.

Here is a similar one: 30 minus 4 times 5 plus 6. Multiply first: 4 times 5 equals 20. Now the sum reads 30 minus 20 plus 6. Going from left to right, 30 minus 20 equals 10, and then 10 plus 6 equals 16.
steps: Multiplication is done before subtraction and addition, so start with 3 times 7, which is 21.
Now the sum reads 48 minus 21 plus 14. Go from left to right and subtract first: 48 minus 21 equals 27.
Then add the 14: 27 plus 14 equals 41. The answer is 41.

Q_CH01_010.q: Using digits 7, 0, 3, 5, each used once, the largest 4-digit number is:
hints: To make the largest number, the biggest digits must sit in the places that are worth the most. The thousands place matters most, then hundreds, then tens, then ones.
Put the digits 7, 0, 3 and 5 in order from biggest to smallest. Then write them from left to right in that order.
Here is a similar one with the digits 4, 9, 0 and 6. From biggest to smallest they are 9, 6, 4, 0, so the largest number is 9,640.
steps: Order the digits from biggest to smallest: 7, 5, 3, 0.
Put the biggest digit in the thousands place and carry on in order: 7 thousands, 5 hundreds, 3 tens and 0 ones.
The largest 4-digit number is 7,530.

hints: The predecessor of a number is the number that comes just before it when you count.
To find the number just before, take away 1 from 10,000. Think what happens to all those zeros when you take 1 away.
Here is a similar one. The predecessor of 1,000 is 1,000 minus 1, which is 999. All the zeros turn into 9s and the number has one digit fewer.
steps: The predecessor is the number just before, so subtract 1. 10000 minus 1 equals 9999.
The predecessor of 10,000 is 9,999.

Q_CH01_012.q: The difference between the place value and face value of 5 in 4,562 is:
hints: Every digit has a face value and a place value. The face value is the digit itself. The place value depends on where it sits.
Find the place of the 5 in 4,562 to get its place value. Its face value is just 5. Then subtract the face value from the place value.
Here is a similar one. In 3,817 the 8 is in the hundreds place, so its place value is 800. Its face value is 8. The difference is 800 minus 8, which is 792.
steps: In 4,562 the 5 is in the hundreds place, so its place value is 500.
The face value of 5 is just 5.
Subtract the face value from the place value. 500 minus 5 equals 495.
The difference is 495.

Q_CH01_013.q: Which of the following is not a valid Roman numeral?
hints: V, which is 5, cannot come before X, which is 10, to subtract. Only I, X and C can be subtracted.
V, L and D are never subtracted. They can't appear before a larger numeral.
V X is invalid. You write 5 as V, not V X.
steps: Rule: V, L and D cannot be used for subtraction.
V X is not valid.

Q_CH01_014.q: Estimate the sum 4,891 plus 3,207 to the nearest thousand.
hints: To estimate a sum, round each number first and then add the rounded numbers.
Round 4,891 to the nearest thousand by looking at its hundreds digit. Do the same for 3,207. If the hundreds digit is 5 or more, round up.
Here is a similar one. Estimate 1,812 plus 4,239. 1,812 rounds up to 2,000 because its hundreds digit is 8. 4,239 rounds down to 4,000 because its hundreds digit is 2. 2,000 plus 4,000 equals 6,000.
steps: Round 4,891. The hundreds digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so round up to 5,000.
Round 3,207. The hundreds digit is 2, which is less than 5, so round down to 3,000.
Add the rounded numbers. 5000 plus 3000 equals 8000.
The estimated sum is 8,000.

options: Twenty-three lakh forty-five thousand six hundred seventy-eight.
Two crore thirty-four lakh fifty-six thousand seventy-eight.
Two million three hundred forty-five thousand six hundred seventy-eight.
Twenty-three crore forty-five lakh six hundred seventy-eight.
hints: In the Indian system the commas split a number into periods: ones, thousands, lakhs and crores. Read one period at a time.
Look at the commas in 23,45,678. From the right, the first group is the ones period, the next is thousands and the next is lakhs. Say each group with its period name.
Here is a similar one. 51,06,342 has 51 in the lakhs period, 06 in the thousands period and 342 in the ones period. It is read as fifty-one lakh six thousand three hundred forty-two.
steps: Split the number at its commas: 23, 45 and 678.
23 is in the lakhs period, 45 is in the thousands period and 678 is in the ones period.
Read each group with its period name. The number is twenty-three lakh forty-five thousand six hundred seventy-eight.

Q_CH01_016.q: How many even numbers are there between 11 and 21?
hints: Even numbers are the ones you say when you count in 2s. Between means the numbers after 11 and before 21.
Write out the numbers from 12 to 20. Then circle the ones that can be split into two equal groups.
Here is a similar one. The even numbers between 3 and 11 are 4, 6, 8 and 10. That makes 4 even numbers.
steps: The numbers between 11 and 21 are 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 20.
The even ones are 12, 14, 16, 18 and 20.
Count them. There are 5 even numbers.

Q_CH01_017.q: The smallest 5-digit number using digits 9, 0, 3, 1, 7, each once, is:
hints: To make the smallest number, the smallest digits go in the places that are worth the most. There is one catch: a number cannot begin with 0.
Choose the smallest digit that is not 0 for the first place. Then write the remaining digits from smallest to biggest. 0 can be used now.
Here is a similar one with the digits 6, 0, 2, 8 and 4. The first digit is 2, the smallest that is not 0. The rest in order are 0, 4, 6, 8, so the smallest number is 20,468.
steps: The first digit cannot be 0, so use the next smallest digit, which is 1.
Write the digits that are left from smallest to biggest: 0, 3, 7, 9.
The smallest 5-digit number is 10,379.

hints: The smallest number with a given number of digits has the smallest digit allowed in front, and every other digit as small as possible.
A number cannot begin with 0, so the first digit must be 1. Fill every other place with the smallest digit there is, and check that you have six digits.
Here is a similar one: the smallest 4-digit number is a 1 followed by three 0s, which is 1,000. It is 1 more than 999, the largest 3-digit number.
steps: The first digit must be 1, because a number cannot begin with 0.
Each of the other five places gets the smallest digit, 0. That gives a 1 followed by five 0s.
As a check, it is 1 more than the largest 5-digit number. 99999 plus 1 equals 100000.
The smallest 6-digit number is 1,00,000, which is one lakh.

Q_CH01_020.q: What is M C M X C I X in Hindu-Arabic numerals?
hints: To read a Roman numeral, break it into parts. When a smaller letter stands before a bigger one, you subtract it.
Split M C M X C I X into M, C M, X C and I X. Work out each part, then add the parts.
Here is a similar one. M C D X L I V splits into M, C D, X L and I V. That is 1000 plus 400 plus 40 plus 4, which is 1444.
steps: Split M C M X C I X into M, C M, X C and I X.
M is 1000. C M is 900. X C is 90. I X is 9.
Add the parts. 1000 plus 900 plus 90 plus 9 equals 1999.
M C M X C I X is 1,999.

hints: A number that lies between two numbers is bigger than the first and smaller than the second.
The two numbers are the same until the last digits. Look at just the endings, 678 and 680, and think what comes between them.
Here is a similar one. Which number lies between 5,21,348 and 5,21,350? Only the endings differ, 348 and 350. The number between them ends in 349, so it is 5,21,349.
steps: Both numbers start with 3,45. Only the endings differ: 678 and 680.
The only whole number between 678 and 680 is 679.
So the number that lies between them is 3,45,679.

hints: This sum has a subtraction, a multiplication and an addition all together. Think about which of the three has to be done first, before you go from left to right.
Work out 3 times 7 first and put that number in its place. Then do the subtraction and the addition in order from left to right.

Here is a similar one: 50 minus 3 times 9 plus 2. Multiply first: 3 times 9 equals 27. Now the sum reads 50 minus 27 plus 2. Going from left to right, 50 minus 27 equals 23, and then 23 plus 2 equals 25.
steps: Multiplication is done before subtraction and addition, so start with 3 times 7, which is 21.
Now the sum reads 25 minus 21 plus 1. Go from left to right and subtract first: 25 minus 21 equals 4.
Then add the 1: 4 plus 1 equals 5. The answer is 5.

Q_CH01_022.q: The product of place value of 4 and face value of 7 in 4,372 is:
hints: Place value depends on where a digit sits. Face value is just the digit itself. Product means you multiply.
Find the place of the 4 in 4,372 to get its place value. The face value of 7 is simply 7. Then multiply the two.
Here is a similar one. In 6,243 the place value of 6 is 6,000 and the face value of 4 is 4. The product is 6,000 times 4, which is 24,000.
steps: In 4,372 the 4 is in the thousands place, so its place value is 4,000.
The face value of 7 is 7.
Multiply them. 4000 times 7 equals 28000.
The product is 28,000.

Q_CH01_023.q: How many zeros are in 5 crore?
hints: Think about how a crore is written in digits. Then count its zeros.
Build up step by step: 1 thousand has 3 zeros and 1 lakh has 5 zeros. Keep going to 10 lakh and then 1 crore. Then swap the 1 for a 5.
Here is a similar one. 1 lakh is written 1,00,000, so 3 lakh is 3,00,000. Count the zeros and you get 5.
steps: 1 crore is written 1,00,00,000. It is a 1 followed by 7 zeros.
5 crore is written 5,00,00,000. The 1 becomes a 5, and the zeros stay the same.
So 5 crore has 7 zeros.

Q_CH01_024.q: A number has 4 in ten-thousands place, 0 in thousands, 3 in hundreds, 0 in tens, and 8 in ones. The number is:
hints: Each digit has its own place. Fill in the places in order, from ten-thousands down to ones.
Draw five boxes for ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. Write each digit in its box. A zero still needs its box.
Here is a similar one. A number has 7 in ten-thousands, 2 in thousands, 0 in hundreds, 5 in tens and 0 in ones. Writing the digits in order gives 72,050.
steps: Write the digits in order of their places: 4 in ten-thousands, 0 in thousands, 3 in hundreds, 0 in tens, 8 in ones.
Add up the values of the digits. 40000 plus 300 plus 8 equals 40308.
The number is 40,308.

hints: To compare two numbers with the same number of digits, start from the left and look for the first place where the digits differ.
Both numbers begin with 65. Now look at the hundreds digits of 65,432 and 65,342 and see which is bigger.
Here is a similar one. Compare 48,715 and 48,175. Both begin with 48. The hundreds digits are 7 and 1, and 7 is bigger, so 48,715 is greater than 48,175.
steps: Both numbers have five digits and both start with 65.
The hundreds digits are 4 and 3. Since 4 is more than 3, the first number is bigger.
So 65,432 is greater than 65,342. The sign is the greater than sign.

hints: The multiples of a number are the answers in its times table. The 8th multiple is the 8th number in that table.
Count along the 9 times table: 9, 18, 27 and so on, until you reach the 8th number. Or multiply 9 by 8.
Example: the 6th multiple of 7 is 7 times 6, which is 42.
steps: The multiples of 9 are 9 times 1, 9 times 2, 9 times 3 and so on.
The 8th multiple is 9 times 8. 9 times 8 equals 72.
The 8th multiple of 9 is 72.

hints: The number just before is one less. So this is a subtraction of 1.
Take 1 away from 50,00,000. Think what happens to the zeros and to the 5 when you take away 1.
Here is a similar one. The number just before 20,000 is 20,000 minus 1, which is 19,999. The 2 drops to 1 and every zero becomes a 9.
steps: The number just before is 1 less, so subtract 1. 5000000 minus 1 equals 4999999.
Written with Indian commas, the number just before 50,00,000 is 49,99,999.

Q_CH01_028.q: The largest 4-digit even number using 5, 3, 8, 1, each once, is:
hints: There are two conditions: the number must be even, and it must be as large as possible. Deal with the even condition first, because it fixes one of the places.
An even number ends in an even digit. Find the even digits among 5, 3, 8 and 1 and decide what must go in the ones place. Then arrange the rest from biggest to smallest.
Here is a similar one with the digits 7, 9, 4 and 3. The only even digit is 4, so it goes in the ones place. The rest from biggest to smallest are 9, 7, 3, so the largest even number is 9,734.
steps: An even number ends in an even digit. Among 5, 3, 8 and 1 the only even digit is 8, so 8 must go in the ones place.
Arrange the other digits in front from biggest to smallest: 5, 3, 1.
The largest 4-digit even number is 5,318. Putting 8 first would leave an odd digit at the end.

Q_CH01_029.q: X I V plus X X V I I I equals what?
options: X X X X I I
hints: Roman numerals are hard to add as they stand. Change each one into ordinary numbers, add, and then change the total back.
Read X I V as a ten and then I V. Read X X V I I I as two tens, a five and three ones. Add the two numbers you get.
Here is a similar one: X V I plus X X I X. X V I is 16 and X X I X is 29, and 16 plus 29 equals 45. Then 45 is 40 and 5, which is X L and V, so the total is X L V.
steps: X I V is a ten and a four. 10 plus 4 equals 14.
X X V I I I is two tens, a five and three ones. 10 plus 10 plus 5 plus 3 equals 28.
Add the two numbers. 14 plus 28 equals 42.
42 is 40 and 2. 40 is X L and 2 is I I, so the total is X L I I.

hints: List all factors: numbers that divide 12 exactly.
Count them: 6 factors.
steps: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.

hints: This is a subtraction. You are finding what is left when one amount is taken away.
Start at 62 and count back 3. Or take away 2 first to reach a round number, then take away the rest.
Here is a similar one: 81 minus 4. Take away 1 to reach 80, then take away 3 more. So 81 minus 4 equals 77.
steps: Take away 2 first to reach a round number. 62 minus 2 equals 60.
3 is 2 and 1, so take away 1 more. 60 minus 1 equals 59.
62 minus 3 equals 59.

Q_CH06_002.q: Which of the following is a prime number?
hints: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. So look for the number that no smaller number, other than 1, divides.
Test each number with small divisors such as 3 and 5. A number ending in 5 can always be divided by 5.
Example: is 39 or 37 prime? 39 equals 3 times 13, so it is not prime. 37 cannot be divided by 2, 3 or 5, so 37 is prime.
steps: 35 and 15 end in 5, so 5 divides them: 35 equals 5 times 7 and 15 equals 3 times 5. They are not prime.
21 equals 3 times 7, so 21 is not prime either.
29 is odd, its digits add up to 11 so 3 does not divide it, and it does not end in 0 or 5. 7 does not divide it either, because 7 times 4 equals 28. So the prime number is 29.

hints: There is a quick test for 3 that uses the digits. A number is divisible by 3 when the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.
Add the four digits of each number. Then check which total is in the 3 times table.
Example: is 4,362 divisible by 3? 4 plus 3 plus 6 plus 2 equals 15, and 15 divided by 3 equals 5, so yes. Is 2,518? 2 plus 5 plus 1 plus 8 equals 16, which is not in the 3 times table, so no.
steps: A number is divisible by 3 when the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. So add the digits of each number.
5,123 gives 5 plus 1 plus 2 plus 3, which is 11. 4,532 gives 14 and 8,206 gives 16. None of these totals is in the 3 times table.
7,251 gives 7 plus 2 plus 5 plus 1, which is 15,, and 15 divided by 3 equals 5. So the number divisible by 3 is 7,251.

hints: This is an addition. You are putting two amounts together.
Add the tens, 60 plus 40. Add the ones, 3 plus 3. Then put the two answers together.
Here is a similar one: 52 plus 34. Tens: 50 plus 30 equals 80. Ones: 2 plus 4 equals 6. So 52 plus 34 equals 86.
steps: Add the tens. 60 plus 40 equals 100.
Add the ones. 3 plus 3 equals 6.
Put them together. 100 plus 6 equals 106.
63 plus 43 equals 106.

hints: There is a quick test for 4. You only need to look at the number made by the last two digits.
Write down the last two digits of each number. Then check which of those two-digit numbers is in the 4 times table.
Example: is 5,728 divisible by 4? Its last two digits make 28, and 28 divided by 4 equals 7, so yes. Is 6,142? Its last two digits make 42, which is not in the 4 times table, so no.
steps: A number is divisible by 4 when its last two digits make a number divisible by 4.
The last two digits of the four numbers are 16, 34, 31 and 18. 34, 31 and 18 are not in the 4 times table.
16 divided by 4 equals 4, with nothing left over. So the number divisible by 4 is 2,316.

Q_CH06_005.q: The H C F of 12 and 18 is:
hints: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. The factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 18.
The common factors are 1, 2, 3 and 6. The highest is 6.
The H C F is 6.
steps: The common factors are 1, 2, 3 and 6.
The H C F is 6.

Q_CH06_006.q: The L C M of 6 and 8 is:
hints: The L C M is the smallest number that is a multiple of both numbers. Listing multiples is a good way to find it.
Write out the multiples of 8, starting 8, 16. Stop at the first one that 6 also divides.
Example: the L C M of 4 and 6. The multiples of 6 are 6, 12. The number 12 is also a multiple of 4, so the L C M of 4 and 6 is 12.
steps: List the multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30.
List the multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32.
The first number that is in both lists is 24. The L C M of 6 and 8 is 24.

hints: This is a multiplication. It means equal groups added together.
19 is 1 less than 20. Work out 20 times 43 first, then take away one 43.
Here is a similar one: 19 times 32. 20 times 32 equals 640. Take away one 32: 640 minus 32 equals 608. So 19 times 32 equals 608.
steps: Work out 20 lots of 43. 20 times 43 equals 860.
19 lots is one lot fewer, so take away 43. 860 minus 43 equals 817.
19 times 43 equals 817.

hints: A prime factorization writes a number as a product of prime numbers only. Every number in the product must be prime.
Start by dividing 60 by the smallest prime, 2. Keep splitting any part that is not prime.
Example: 84 equals 2 times 42, then 42 equals 2 times 21, then 21 equals 3 times 7. So the prime factorization of 84 is 2 times 2 times 3 times 7.
steps: Split 60 using the smallest prime: 60 equals 2 times 30.
30 is not prime, so split again: 30 equals 2 times 15. Then 15 equals 3 times 5.
Now every part is prime. The prime factorization of 60 is 2 times 2 times 3 times 5. 2 times 2 times 3 times 5 equals 60.

Q_CH06_008.q: A number divisible by 6 must be divisible by:
hints: Think about which smaller numbers multiply to make 6. Every multiple of 6 is also a multiple of those numbers.
Write 6 as a product of two smaller numbers. Then test your idea with a multiple of 6, such as 18.
Example: 10 equals 2 times 5, so a number divisible by 10 must be divisible by 2 and by 5. Check with 30: 30 divided by 2 equals 15 and 30 divided by 5 equals 6.
steps: Write 6 as a product. 2 times 3 equals 6.
So every multiple of 6 is a multiple of 2 and also of 3. Check with 18: 18 divided by 2 equals 9 and 18 divided by 3 equals 6.
A number divisible by 6 must be divisible by 2 and 3.

hints: This is a multiplication. It means equal groups added together.
99 is 1 less than 100. Work out 100 times 39 first, then take away one 39.
Here is a similar one: 99 times 24. 100 times 24 equals 2400. Take away one 24: 2400 minus 24 equals 2376. So 99 times 24 equals 2376.
steps: Work out 100 lots of 39. 100 times 39 equals 3900.
99 lots is one lot fewer, so take away 39. 3900 minus 39 equals 3861.
99 times 39 equals 3861.

hints: This is a subtraction. You are finding what is left when one amount is taken away.
50 is 5 tens, so only the tens digit changes. Take 5 tens from 9 tens.
Here is a similar one: 86 minus 30. 8 tens take away 3 tens leaves 5 tens, and the 6 ones stay. So 86 minus 30 equals 56.
steps: Take the tens away. 90 minus 50 equals 40.
The 7 ones stay as they are. 40 plus 7 equals 47.
97 minus 50 equals 47.

Q_CH06_009.q: Which pair of numbers is co-prime?
hints: Co-prime means the H C F is 1: no common factor except 1.
8 and 12: the H C F is 4. 15 and 35: the H C F is 5. 6 and 9: the H C F is 3. 9 and 16: the factors of 9 are 1, 3, 9, and the factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The only common factor is 1.
9 and 16 are co-prime.
steps: The H C F of 9 and 16 is 1.

hints: Digit sum: 4 plus 5 plus 1 plus 8 equals 18. Is 18 divisible by 9?
18 divided by 9 equals 2. Yes!
4,518 is divisible by 9.
steps: 4 plus 5 plus 1 plus 8 equals 18. 18 divided by 9 equals 2.

hints: This is a multiplication. It means equal groups added together.
Think of 3 groups of 3. Add 3 plus 3 plus 3, or say the 3 times table.
Here is a similar one: 4 times 4 means 4 groups of 4. 4 plus 4 plus 4 plus 4 equals 16, so 4 times 4 equals 16.
steps: 3 times 3 means 3 groups of 3. Add them up. 3 plus 3 plus 3 equals 9.
3 times 3 equals 9.

hints: Composite means it has more than 2 factors. 1 is neither. 2 and 3 are prime.
4 equals 2 times 2. It has the factors 1, 2 and 4. More than 2 factors!
4 is the smallest composite.
steps: 4 has the factors 1, 2 and 4. 3 factors is more than 2.

hints: There is a test for 11 that uses the digits in turn. You add every other digit to make two totals, and then compare the two totals.
Add the 1st and 3rd digits, 8 and 9. Add the 2nd and 4th digits, 2 and 4. Then find the difference between the two totals.

Example: is 3,729 divisible by 11? 3 plus 2 equals 5 and 7 plus 9 equals 16. The difference is 16 minus 5, which is 11, a multiple of 11, so 3,729 is divisible by 11. Check: 11 times 339 equals 3,729.
steps: For 11, add the digits in the 1st and 3rd places: 8 plus 9 equals 17.
Add the digits in the 2nd and 4th places: 2 plus 4 equals 6.
The difference is 17 minus 6, which is 11. When this difference is 0 or a multiple of 11, the number is divisible by 11.
Check: 11 times 754 equals 8,294. Yes, 8,294 is divisible by 11.

Q_CH06_013.q: Two bells ring every 12 and 18 minutes. If they ring together at 9:00 a m, when will they ring together again?
hints: The bells ring together whenever the minutes passed are a multiple of both gaps. The first time this happens is the smallest common multiple, the L C M.
List the multiples of 18, starting with 18 itself. Stop at the first one that is also a multiple of 12.

Example: two bells ring every 10 and 15 minutes and ring together at 8:00 a m. The multiples of 15 are 15, 30, and 30 is also a multiple of 10. So they ring together again 30 minutes later, at 8 30 a m.
steps: The first bell rings after 12, 24, 36 and 48 minutes. The second bell rings after 18, 36 and 54 minutes.
The first number in both lists is 36, so the L C M of 12 and 18 is 36. The bells ring together 36 minutes after 9:00 a m.
36 minutes after 9:00 a m is 9 36 a m. The bells ring together again at 9 36 a m.

hints: This is a multiplication. It means equal groups added together.
50 is half of 100. Work out 100 times 47 first, then halve it.
Here is a similar one: 50 times 26. 100 times 26 equals 2600, and half of 2600 is 1300. So 50 times 26 equals 1300.
steps: Work out 100 lots of 47. 100 times 47 equals 4700.
50 is half of 100, so halve the answer. 4700 divided by 2 equals 2350.
50 times 47 equals 2350.

Q_CH06_014.q: 48 apples and 36 oranges are to be packed in boxes. Each box must have the same number of fruits, all of the same type. What is the maximum number of fruits in each box?
hints: Every box holds the same number of fruits, and nothing may be left over. So the number in a box must divide both totals, and you want the largest such number.
List the factors of 36, the smaller number. Then test them on 48, starting from the largest.

Example: 40 pens and 30 pencils go into packets of equal size, one kind per packet. The factors of 30 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15 and 30. Testing from the largest, 30 and 15 do not divide 40, but 10 does. So each packet holds 10.
steps: The number of fruits in a box must divide both 48 and 36 exactly. The largest such number is the H C F of 48 and 36.
The factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18 and 36. Testing from the largest, 36 and 18 do not divide 48, but 12 does.
48 divided by 12 equals 4 boxes of apples and 36 divided by 12 equals 3 boxes of oranges. The maximum number of fruits in each box is 12.

Q_CH06_015.q: Which of these is a pair of twin primes?
hints: Twin primes are two prime numbers that are exactly 2 apart.
For each pair, check two things. Are both numbers prime? Is their difference 2?
Example: 5 and 7 are both prime and 7 minus 5 equals 2, so they are twin primes. 7 and 9 are also 2 apart, but 9, which is 3 times 3, is not prime, so they are not twin primes.
steps: Twin primes are two primes with a difference of 2.
Find each difference: 17 minus 13 equals 4, 7 minus 3 equals 4, 13 minus 11 equals 2 and 13 minus 7 equals 6.
Only one pair is 2 apart, and both of its numbers are prime.
The twin primes are 11 and 13.

hints: This is an addition. You are putting two amounts together.
Start at 15 and count on 2 more.
Here is a similar one: 24 plus 3. Count on from 24: 25, 26, 27. So 24 plus 3 equals 27.
steps: Add the ones. 5 plus 2 equals 7.
Keep the 1 ten and put the 7 ones with it. 10 plus 7 equals 17.
15 plus 2 equals 17.

hints: There is a test for 8 that uses only the end of the number. Look at the number made by the last three digits.
Write down the last three digits of each number. Then divide each of those three-digit numbers by 8 and see which one leaves nothing over.
Example: is 3,128 divisible by 8? Its last three digits make 128, and 128 divided by 8 equals 16, so yes. Is 4,620? Its last three digits make 620, and 620 divided by 8 leaves 4 over, so no.
steps: A number is divisible by 8 when its last three digits make a number divisible by 8.
The last three digits of the four numbers are 214, 234, 648 and 342. Dividing by 8, 214 leaves 6 over, 234 leaves 2 over and 342 leaves 6 over.
648 divided by 8 equals 81 exactly. So the number divisible by 8 is 5,648.

hints: This is an addition. You are putting two amounts together.
98 is close to 100. Move 2 from the 47 over to the 98 to make the sum easier.
Here is a similar one: 97 plus 36. Move 3 from the 36 to the 97. That makes 100 plus 33, which is 133. So 97 plus 36 equals 133.
steps: Take 2 from the 47 and give it to the 98. 98 plus 2 equals 100.
The 47 has become 45. 47 minus 2 equals 45.
Add the easy numbers. 100 plus 45 equals 145.
98 plus 47 equals 145.

Q_CH06_017.q: A number has exactly 2 factors. This number must be:
hints: Numbers get different names depending on how many factors they have. Think about which name goes with exactly two.
Try a few small numbers. Write all the factors of 5, of 6 and of 1, and count them.
Example: 7 has the factors 1 and 7, which is exactly two. 8 has the factors 1, 2, 4 and 8, which is four. So 7 and 8 are different kinds of number.
steps: A number with exactly 2 factors can be divided only by 1 and by itself.
For example, 5 has just the factors 1 and 5.
A number like this is called prime.

Q_CH06_018.q: 6 is called a perfect number because:
options: it equals the sum of its factors, excluding itself: 1 plus 2 plus 3 equals 6
hints: A perfect number has a special link with its own factors. Think about what happens when you add up the factors that are smaller than the number.
List the factors of 6. Leave out 6 itself and add the others.
Example: 28 is also a perfect number. Its factors, leaving out 28 itself, are 1, 2, 4, 7 and 14, and 1 plus 2 plus 4 plus 7 plus 14 equals 28.
steps: The factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6.
Leave out 6 itself. The factors that remain are 1, 2 and 3.
Add them up. 6 is called perfect because it equals the sum of its factors, excluding itself: 1 plus 2 plus 3 equals 6.

Q_CH06_019.q: A number is divisible by 5 if its last digit is:
hints: Look at the 5 times table and watch the last digit of each answer.
Write out the first few multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20 and so on. What do you notice about the ones digit?
Example: the rule for 2. The multiples of 2 are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and so on. Their last digits are always 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. So 134 is divisible by 2 and 137 is not.
steps: The multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and so on.
Their last digits go 5, 0, 5, 0, again and again.
So a number is divisible by 5 if its last digit is 0 or 5.

Q_CH06_020.q: The first three common multiples of 4 and 6 are:
hints: A common multiple is a number that is in both times tables. You need the first three of them.
Write the multiples of 4 in one row and the multiples of 6 in another. Circle the numbers that appear in both rows.
Example: 2 and 5. The multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. The ones that are also in the 2 times table are 10, 20 and 30. Those are the first three common multiples.
steps: Look for the numbers that are in both lists.
The first three common multiples are 12, 24, 36.

Q_CH06_021.q: If the H C F of two numbers is 6 and their L C M is 36, and one number is 12, find the other.
hints: This uses a special rule for two numbers: H C F times L C M is equal to the product of the two numbers.
Multiply the H C F by the L C M. That gives the product of the two numbers. Then think how to get the missing number from it.
Example: H C F equals 5, L C M equals 60 and one number is 15. 5 times 60 equals 300. Then 300 divided by 15 equals 20. The other number is 20.
steps: H C F times L C M gives the product of the two numbers. 6 times 36 equals 216.
Divide this product by the number you know. 216 divided by 12 equals 18.
The other number is 18.

hints: There is a quick test for 10. You only need to look at one digit of each number.
Think of the 10 times table: 10, 20, 30 and so on. What is the last digit every time? Check the last digit of each choice.
Example: 4,570 ends in 0, so it is divisible by 10. 4,575 ends in 5, so it is not.
steps: A number is divisible by 10 when its last digit is 0.
7,105 ends in 5. 8,901 ends in 1. 4,055 ends in 5.
3,200 ends in 0. So 3,200 is divisible by 10. 3200 divided by 10 equals 320.

hints: This is an addition. You are putting two amounts together.
Add the ones first, 3 plus 6. The tens stay the same.
Here is a similar one: 42 plus 7. The ones are 2 plus 7, which is 9, and the 4 tens stay. So 42 plus 7 equals 49.
steps: Add the ones. 3 plus 6 equals 9.
Keep the 6 tens and put the 9 ones with them. 60 plus 9 equals 69.
63 plus 6 equals 69.

Q_CH06_023.q: How many prime numbers are there between 10 and 20?
hints: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. Check each number between 10 and 20.
Cross out the even numbers first, since 2 divides them. Then test the odd numbers that are left with 3 and 5.
Example: the primes between 90 and 100. The even numbers are out. 91 equals 7 times 13, 93 equals 3 times 31, 95 equals 5 times 19 and 99 equals 9 times 11. Only 97 is left, so there is 1 prime.
steps: Look at the numbers from 11 to 19.
12, 14, 16 and 18 are even, and 15 equals 3 times 5. None of these is prime.
11, 13, 17 and 19 have no factors other than 1 and themselves.
There are 4 prime numbers.

Q_CH06_024.q: The only even prime number is:
hints: A prime number has exactly two factors. Even numbers are the ones in the 2 times table.
List the factors of each choice. Look for the one whose only factors are 1 and itself.
Example: is 9 prime? 9 equals 3 times 3, so 9 has the factors 1, 3 and 9. That is three factors, so 9 is not prime.
steps: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
2 has only the factors 1 and 2, so 2 is prime.
Every other even number can be divided by 2 as well as by 1 and itself. So it has more than two factors.
The only even prime number is 2.

hints: This is a subtraction. You are finding what is left when one amount is taken away.
Start at 7 and count back 5 steps on your fingers.
Here is a similar one: 9 minus 6. Start at 9 and count back 6 steps: 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3. So 9 minus 6 equals 3.
steps: Start at 7 and count back 5 steps: 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. 7 minus 5 equals 2.
7 minus 5 equals 2.

hints: This is a subtraction. You are finding what is left when one amount is taken away.
The two numbers are close together. Count up from 41 until you reach 46.
Here is a similar one: 58 minus 54. Count up from 54: 55, 56, 57, 58. That is 4 steps, so 58 minus 54 equals 4.
steps: Count up from 41 to 46: 42, 43, 44, 45, 46. That is 5 steps. 41 plus 5 equals 46.
So 46 minus 41 equals 5.

Q_CH06_025.q: In the Sieve of Eratosthenes, after crossing out multiples of 2, 3, 5, and 7, all remaining numbers up to 50 are:
hints: The Sieve of Eratosthenes is a way of sorting numbers. Think about what kind of number gets crossed out.
A number that is crossed out is a multiple of a smaller number, so it has extra factors. What do we call numbers that have no extra factors?
Example: on a grid from 2 to 10, keep 2 and cross out its other multiples: 4, 6, 8 and 10. Keep 3 and cross out 9. The numbers left are 2, 3, 5 and 7. Each has only two factors.
steps: In the sieve we keep 2, 3, 5 and 7 and cross out all their other multiples.
Every composite number up to 50 is a multiple of 2, 3, 5 or 7, so it gets crossed out.
The numbers left are prime numbers.

Q_CH07_001.q: Which of the following are like fractions?
hints: Like fractions are fractions whose bottom numbers are all the same. The top numbers can be different.
Look only at the bottom numbers in each group. Find the group where they all match.
Example: 1 over 9, 4 over 9 and 7 over 9 are like fractions because every bottom number is 9. But 1 over 3, 1 over 5 and 1 over 8 are not, because their bottom numbers are different.
steps: Like fractions have the same bottom number, which is called the denominator.
In 1 over 2, 1 over 3 and 1 over 4, the tops match, but the bottoms are 2, 3 and 4. The groups 2 over 3, 4 over 5, 1 over 6, and 3 over 7, 5 over 9, 2 over 11, have different bottoms as well.
Only one group has the same bottom number, 5, in every fraction. The like fractions are 2 over 5, 3 over 5 and 4 over 5.

Q_CH07_002.q: Which is the largest: 3 over 7, 5 over 7, 2 over 7 or 6 over 7?
hints: All four fractions have the same bottom number, so the pieces are all the same size. Only the number of pieces differs.
Compare the top numbers 3, 5, 2 and 6. More pieces of the same size make a bigger fraction.
Example: in 2 over 9, 8 over 9, 4 over 9 and 5 over 9 the pieces are all ninths. 8 is the biggest top number, so 8 over 9 is the largest.
steps: Every fraction has 7 below, so each one counts sevenths, and the pieces are the same size.
The tops are 3, 5, 2 and 6. The biggest top number is 6, which means the most pieces.
The largest fraction is 6 over 7.

Q_CH07_003.q: Which is the smallest: 3 over 4, 3 over 8, 3 over 5 or 3 over 2?
hints: All four fractions have the same top number, so each has the same number of pieces. What changes is the size of each piece.
Think about cutting a whole into 2, 4, 5 or 8 equal pieces. Decide which cut gives the smallest pieces.
Example: in 2 over 3, 2 over 9, 2 over 5 and 2 over 7, each fraction has 2 pieces. Ninths are the smallest pieces, so 2 over 9 is the smallest fraction.
steps: Every fraction has 3 pieces. The bottom number tells how many equal pieces the whole is cut into.
The more pieces a whole is cut into, the smaller each piece is. Eighths are smaller than fifths, quarters and halves.
So 3 eighths is the least amount. The smallest fraction is 3 over 8.

Q_CH07_004.q: Convert 3 and 2 over 5 to an improper fraction.
hints: An improper fraction counts everything in the same size of piece. Here that means turning the whole numbers into fifths too.
Each whole is 5 fifths. Find how many fifths there are in 3 wholes.
Example: 2 and three quarters. Two wholes are 2 times 4, which is 8 quarters. Adding the 3 extra quarters gives 8 plus 3, which is 11, so 2 and three quarters equals 11 over 4.
steps: Each whole is 5 fifths, so 3 wholes are 3 times 5, which is 15 fifths.
Add the 2 extra fifths: 15 plus 2 equals 17 fifths.
So 3 and 2 over 5 equals 17 over 5.

Q_CH07_005.q: Convert 23 over 4 to a mixed number.
hints: To change an improper fraction into a mixed number, divide the top by the bottom. The quotient is the whole part and the remainder becomes the new top.
Divide 23 by 4. Find how many whole 4s fit into 23 and how much is left over.
Example: 19 over 6. 6 times 3 equals 18, so 6 fits 3 times with 19 minus 18, which is 1 left over. So 19 over 6 equals 3 and 1 over 6.
steps: Divide 23 by 4. 4 times 5 equals 20 and 4 times 6 equals 24, so 4 fits into 23 five whole times.
The remainder is 23 minus 20, which is 3.
The whole part is 5 and the 3 left over are quarters. So 23 over 4 equals 5 and three quarters.

hints: Both fractions are eighths, so the pieces are the same size. Adding them means counting the pieces altogether.
Add the top numbers 3 and 5 and keep 8 at the bottom. Then look at what that fraction equals.
Example: 2 over 6, plus 3 over 6. The tops give 2 plus 3, which is 5, and the bottom stays 6, so the sum is 5 over 6.
steps: Both fractions are eighths. Add the tops and keep the bottom: 3 plus 5 equals 8, so the sum is 8 over 8. 3 over 8, plus 5 over 8, equals 8 over 8.
8 eighths make one whole. So 3 over 8, plus 5 over 8, equals 1.

hints: This is a multiplication. It means equal groups added together.
Split 45 into 40 and 5. Multiply 75 by each part, then add the two answers.
Here is a similar one: 25 times 32. 25 times 30 equals 750 and 25 times 2 equals 50. 750 plus 50 equals 800, so 25 times 32 equals 800.
steps: Split 45 into 40 and 5. Multiply 75 by 40. 75 times 40 equals 3000.
Multiply 75 by 5. 75 times 5 equals 375.
Add the two parts. 3000 plus 375 equals 3375.
75 times 45 equals 3375.

hints: Thirds and quarters are pieces of different sizes. Before adding, both fractions must be changed to the same bottom number.
Find the smallest number that both 3 and 4 divide into. Change each fraction so that it has that number at the bottom.
Example: 1 over 2, plus 1 over 3. Both can be written in sixths: 1 over 2 equals 3 over 6 and 1 over 3 equals 2 over 6. Then 3 over 6, plus 2 over 6, equals 5 over 6.
steps: Thirds and quarters are different sizes, so change both into twelfths, because 3 times 4 equals 12.
1 over 3 equals 4 over 12 and 1 over 4 equals 3 over 12.
Add the tops and keep the bottom: 4 plus 3 equals 7. So 1 over 3, plus 1 over 4, equals 7 over 12. 4 over 12, plus 3 over 12, equals 7 over 12.

hints: The two fractions have different bottom numbers. Make the bottoms the same before you subtract.
6 is a multiple of 3. Change 1 over 3 into sixths by multiplying its top and bottom by 2.
Example: 7 over 8, minus 1 over 4. Change 1 over 4 into eighths: 1 over 4 equals 2 over 8. Then 7 over 8, minus 2 over 8, equals 5 over 8.
steps: Change 1 over 3 into sixths. Multiply its top and bottom by 2 to get 2 over 6.
Subtract the tops and keep the bottom: 5 minus 2 equals 3, so the result is 3 over 6. 5 over 6, minus 2 over 6, equals 3 over 6.
Simplify by dividing the top and bottom by 3. So 5 over 6, minus 1 over 3, equals 1 over 2.

hints: This is an addition. You are putting two amounts together.
Add the ones first, 4 plus 3. The tens stay the same.
Here is a similar one: 71 plus 8. The ones are 1 plus 8, which is 9, and the 7 tens stay. So 71 plus 8 equals 79.
steps: Add the ones. 4 plus 3 equals 7.
Keep the 5 tens and put the 7 ones with them. 50 plus 7 equals 57.
54 plus 3 equals 57.

hints: This is a multiplication. It means equal groups added together.
To multiply by 11, multiply by 10 and then add one more group.
Here is a similar one: 7 times 11. 7 times 10 equals 70, and one more 7 makes 77. So 7 times 11 equals 77.
steps: Multiply 9 by 10. 9 times 10 equals 90.
11 groups is one more group of 9. 90 plus 9 equals 99.
9 times 11 equals 99.

hints: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number is the same as finding that fraction of the number.
Find one fifth of 10 first, by dividing 10 by 5. Then take 3 of those parts.
Example: 2 over 3, times 12. One third of 12 is 12 divided by 3, which is 4. Two thirds is 2 times 4, which is 8. So 2 over 3, times 12, equals 8.
steps: 3 over 5, times 10, means three fifths of 10. One fifth of 10 is 10 divided by 5, which is 2.
Three fifths is 3 of those parts: 3 times 2 equals 6.
So 3 over 5, times 10, equals 6.

hints: This is a subtraction. You are finding what is left when one amount is taken away.
30 is 3 tens, so only the tens digit changes. Take 3 tens from 4 tens.
Here is a similar one: 75 minus 20. 7 tens take away 2 tens leaves 5 tens, and the 5 ones stay. So 75 minus 20 equals 55.
steps: Take the tens away. 40 minus 30 equals 10.
The 2 ones stay as they are. 10 plus 2 equals 12.
42 minus 30 equals 12.

hints: The word of here means multiply. To find a fraction of a number, share the number into equal parts and take some of them.
Divide 45 by 3 to find one third. Then think about how many thirds you need.
Example: 3 over 5 of 40. 40 divided by 5 equals 8, and 8 times 3 equals 24. So 3 over 5 of 40 is 24.
steps: One third of 45 is 15. 45 divided by 3 equals 15.
Two thirds is 2 of these parts. 15 times 2 equals 30.
Two thirds of 45 is 30.

Q_CH07_010_V01.q: Vivaan has 12 sweets and gives away one quarter of them. How many sweets does Vivaan give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 12 sweets into 4 equal groups. How many sweets are in one group?
Example: 1 over 5 of 35 sweets. Share 35 into 5 equal groups: 35 divided by 5 equals 7. So 1 over 5 of 35 is 7 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 4, so share the 12 sweets into 4 equal groups. 12 divided by 4 equals 3.
The top number is 1, so Vivaan gives away one of these groups.
Vivaan gives away 3 sweets.

Q_CH07_010_V04.q: Meera has 8 sweets and gives away one half of them. How many sweets does Meera give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 8 sweets into 2 equal groups. How many sweets are in one group?
Example: 1 over 5 of 35 sweets. Share 35 into 5 equal groups: 35 divided by 5 equals 7. So 1 over 5 of 35 is 7 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 2, so share the 8 sweets into 2 equal groups. 8 divided by 2 equals 4.
The top number is 1, so Meera gives away one of these groups.
Meera gives away 4 sweets.

Q_CH07_010_V08.q: Meera has 72 sweets and gives away 5 over 6 of them. How many sweets does Meera give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 72 sweets into 6 equal groups first. Then think about how many of those groups Meera gives away.
Example: 3 over 7 of 14 sweets. Share 14 into 7 equal groups: 14 divided by 7 equals 2. Take 3 of the groups: 2 times 3 equals 6. So 3 over 7 of 14 is 6 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 6, so share the 72 sweets into 6 equal groups. 72 divided by 6 equals 12.
The top number is 5, so Meera gives away 5 of these groups. 12 times 5 equals 60.
Meera gives away 60 sweets.

hints: Equivalent fractions have the same value. You get one by multiplying the top and the bottom by the same number.
Multiply the top and bottom of 3 over 4 by 2, then by 3. See which choice appears.
Example: 2 over 5. Multiply the top and bottom by 3: 2 times 3 equals 6 and 5 times 3 equals 15. So 6 over 15 is equivalent to 2 over 5.
steps: To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top and the bottom by the same number.
Multiply both by 2: 3 times 2 equals 6 and 4 times 2 equals 8. 3 over 4 equals 6 over 8.
The equivalent fraction is 6 over 8.

hints: To simplify a fraction, divide the top and the bottom by the same number. Keep going until no number divides both.
Find the biggest number that divides both 18 and 24. Then divide the top and the bottom by it.
Example: 12 over 20. The biggest number that divides both is 4. 12 divided by 4 equals 3 and 20 divided by 4 equals 5, so 12 over 20 equals 3 over 5.
steps: The biggest number that divides both 18 and 24 is 6.
Divide the top and bottom by 6: 18 divided by 6 equals 3 and 24 divided by 6 equals 4. 18 over 24 equals 3 over 4.
In simplest form the fraction is 3 over 4.

Q_CH07_013.q: Riya ate 2 over 5 of a pizza. 1 over 5 was left over. What fraction was eaten by others?
hints: The whole pizza is 5 over 5. It is split into three parts: what Riya ate, what the others ate and what was left.
Add Riya's share and the leftover share. Then see how many fifths are still missing from 5 over 5.
Example: Arjun ate 3 over 8 of a cake and 2 over 8 was left over. 3 over 8, plus 2 over 8, equals 5 over 8. The others ate the rest: 8 over 8, minus 5 over 8, equals 3 over 8.
steps: The whole pizza is 5 over 5.
Add Riya's share and the leftover. 2 over 5, plus 1 over 5, equals 3 over 5.
Take this away from the whole pizza. 5 over 5, minus 3 over 5, equals 2 over 5.
The others ate 2 over 5 of the pizza.

Q_CH07_013_V03.q: Ananya has 22 sweets and gives away one half of them. How many sweets does Ananya give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 22 sweets into 2 equal groups. How many sweets are in one group?
Example: 1 over 5 of 35 sweets. Share 35 into 5 equal groups: 35 divided by 5 equals 7. So 1 over 5 of 35 is 7 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 2, so share the 22 sweets into 2 equal groups. 22 divided by 2 equals 11.
The top number is 1, so Ananya gives away one of these groups.
Ananya gives away 11 sweets.

Q_CH07_013_V07.q: Ishika has 25 sweets and gives away 3 over 5 of them. How many sweets does Ishika give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 25 sweets into 5 equal groups first. Then think about how many of those groups Ishika gives away.
Example: 5 over 8 of 56 sweets. Share 56 into 8 equal groups: 56 divided by 8 equals 7. Take 5 of the groups: 7 times 5 equals 35. So 5 over 8 of 56 is 35 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 5, so share the 25 sweets into 5 equal groups. 25 divided by 5 equals 5.
The top number is 3, so Ishika gives away 3 of these groups. 5 times 3 equals 15.
Ishika gives away 15 sweets.

Q_CH07_013_V09.q: Kabir has 12 sweets and gives away one quarter of them. How many sweets does Kabir give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 12 sweets into 4 equal groups. How many sweets are in one group?
Example: 1 over 5 of 35 sweets. Share 35 into 5 equal groups: 35 divided by 5 equals 7. So 1 over 5 of 35 is 7 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 4, so share the 12 sweets into 4 equal groups. 12 divided by 4 equals 3.
The top number is 1, so Kabir gives away one of these groups.
Kabir gives away 3 sweets.

Q_CH07_013_V10.q: Saanvi has 18 sweets and gives away one half of them. How many sweets does Saanvi give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 18 sweets into 2 equal groups. How many sweets are in one group?
Example: 1 over 5 of 35 sweets. Share 35 into 5 equal groups: 35 divided by 5 equals 7. So 1 over 5 of 35 is 7 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 2, so share the 18 sweets into 2 equal groups. 18 divided by 2 equals 9.
The top number is 1, so Saanvi gives away one of these groups.
Saanvi gives away 9 sweets.

Q_CH07_014.q: Arrange in ascending order: 2 over 3, 3 over 4, 5 over 6 and 1 over 2.
hints: Ascending means from smallest to largest. To compare fractions with different bottom numbers, change them all to the same bottom number.
Find the smallest number that 3, 4, 6 and 2 all divide into. Write every fraction with that number below.
Example: arrange 1 over 2, 3 over 8 and 3 over 4 in ascending order. In eighths they are 4 over 8, 3 over 8 and 6 over 8. From smallest to largest that is 3 over 8, 1 over 2 and 3 over 4.
steps: The smallest number that 3, 4, 6 and 2 all divide into is 12. So change every fraction into twelfths.
2 over 3 equals 8 over 12, 3 over 4 equals 9 over 12, 5 over 6 equals 10 over 12 and 1 over 2 equals 6 over 12.
Put the tops in order from smallest to largest: 6 over 12, 8 over 12, 9 over 12 and 10 over 12.
In ascending order the fractions are 1 over 2, 2 over 3, 3 over 4 and 5 over 6.

hints: This sum has a subtraction, a multiplication and an addition all together. Think about which of the three has to be done first, before you go from left to right.
Work out 3 times 7 first and put that number in its place. Then do the subtraction and the addition in order from left to right.

Here is a similar one: 30 minus 4 times 5 plus 6. Multiply first: 4 times 5 equals 20. Now the sum reads 30 minus 20 plus 6. Going from left to right, 30 minus 20 equals 10, and then 10 plus 6 equals 16.
steps: Multiplication is done before subtraction and addition, so start with 3 times 7, which is 21.
Now the sum reads 41 minus 21 plus 12. Go from left to right and subtract first: 41 minus 21 equals 20.
Then add the 12: 20 plus 12 equals 32. The answer is 32.

hints: This sum has a subtraction, a multiplication and an addition all together. Think about which of the three has to be done first, before you go from left to right.
Work out 7 times 2 first and put that number in its place. Then do the subtraction and the addition in order from left to right.

Here is a similar one: 30 minus 4 times 5 plus 6. Multiply first: 4 times 5 equals 20. Now the sum reads 30 minus 20 plus 6. Going from left to right, 30 minus 20 equals 10, and then 10 plus 6 equals 16.
steps: Multiplication is done before subtraction and addition, so start with 7 times 2, which is 14.
Now the sum reads 16 minus 14 plus 1. Go from left to right and subtract first: 16 minus 14 equals 2.
Then add the 1: 2 plus 1 equals 3. The answer is 3.

hints: To multiply two fractions, multiply the tops together and the bottoms together. Then simplify the result.
Multiply 2 by 3 for the new top and 3 by 5 for the new bottom. Then look for a number that divides both.
Example: 3 over 4, times 2 over 3. Tops: 3 times 2 equals 6. Bottoms: 4 times 3 equals 12. Then 6 over 12 simplifies to 1 over 2.
steps: Multiply the tops: 2 times 3 equals 6. Multiply the bottoms: 3 times 5 equals 15. That gives 6 over 15.
Both 6 and 15 can be divided by 3: 6 divided by 3 equals 2 and 15 divided by 3 equals 5.
So 2 over 3, times 3 over 5, equals 2 over 5. 6 over 15 equals 2 over 5.

Q_CH07_015_V07.q: Diya has 36 sweets and gives away one quarter of them. How many sweets does Diya give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 36 sweets into 4 equal groups. How many sweets are in one group?
Example: 1 over 5 of 35 sweets. Share 35 into 5 equal groups: 35 divided by 5 equals 7. So 1 over 5 of 35 is 7 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 4, so share the 36 sweets into 4 equal groups. 36 divided by 4 equals 9.
The top number is 1, so Diya gives away one of these groups.
Diya gives away 9 sweets.

Q_CH07_016.q: 2 and a third plus 1 and two thirds equals what?
hints: To add mixed numbers, add the whole numbers and the fractions separately. Then see if the fractions make another whole.
Add the wholes, 2 and 1. Then add the fraction parts, which both have 3 below.
Example: 2 and 2 over 5, plus 3 and 3 over 5. Wholes: 2 plus 3 equals 5. Fractions: 2 over 5, plus 3 over 5, equals 5 over 5, which is 1 whole. Total: 5 plus 1 equals 6.
steps: Add the whole numbers: 2 plus 1 equals 3.
Add the fractions: 1 over 3, plus 2 over 3, equals 3 over 3, which is one whole.
Add the extra whole: 3 plus 1 equals 4. So 2 and a third plus 1 and two thirds equals 4.

Q_CH07_017.q: The reciprocal of 5 over 7 is what?
hints: The reciprocal of a fraction is the fraction turned upside down.
Look at the top and bottom of 5 over 7. Swap their places.
Example: the reciprocal of 3 over 8 is 8 over 3. Check: 3 over 8, times 8 over 3, equals 24 over 24, which is 1.
steps: To find a reciprocal, swap the top and the bottom.
A fraction times its reciprocal is always 1. 5 over 7, times 7 over 5, equals 1.
The reciprocal of 5 over 7 is 7 over 5.

Q_CH07_018.q: Which fraction lies between 0 and 1 over 2?
hints: Use one half as a marker. You are looking for a fraction that is less than half.
For each fraction, double the top and compare it with the bottom. If double the top is smaller than the bottom, the fraction is less than half.
Example: is 2 over 9 between 0 and 1 over 2? Double the top: 2 times 2 equals 4, and 4 is less than 9. So 2 over 9 is less than half.
steps: A fraction is less than half when double its top is smaller than its bottom.
For 3 over 4, 5 over 6 and 7 over 8 the doubled tops are 6, 10 and 14. Each is bigger than the bottom, so these are more than half.
For 1 over 4, 1 times 2 equals 2, which is smaller than 4.
The fraction between 0 and 1 over 2 is 1 over 4.

hints: A unit fraction is one single part of a whole. Think about what its top number must be.
Look at the top number of each fraction. Which fraction means just one part?
Example: 1 over 9 is a unit fraction because its top number is 1. 4 over 9 is not, because its top number is 4.
steps: A unit fraction has 1 as its top number. It is one equal part of a whole.
The top numbers here are 2, 1, 3 and 5.
The unit fraction is 1 over 7.

Q_CH07_020.q: A tank is three quarters full. After using one third of the tank, what fraction is left?
hints: Some of the tank is used, so this is a subtraction. The two fractions have different bottom numbers.
Take 1 over 3 away from 3 over 4. First change both into twelfths, because 4 and 3 both divide into 12.
Example: a jar is 5 over 6 full and one half of the jar is poured out. In sixths, 1 over 2 equals 3 over 6. Then 5 over 6, minus 3 over 6, equals 2 over 6, which is one third of the jar.
steps: Subtract 1 over 3 from 3 over 4. Use twelfths, because 4 and 3 both divide into 12.
Change 3 over 4. 3 over 4 equals 9 over 12.
Change 1 over 3. 1 over 3 equals 4 over 12.
Subtract the tops. 9 over 12, minus 4 over 12, equals 5 over 12.
5 over 12 of the tank is left.

Q_CH07_021.q: Which is greater, 5 over 8 or 3 over 5?
hints: To compare two fractions with different bottom numbers, change them so the bottoms are the same.
8 and 5 both divide into 40. Change 5 over 8 and 3 over 5 into fortieths, then compare the tops.
Example: 2 over 3 or 3 over 4? Use twelfths: 2 over 3 equals 8 over 12 and 3 over 4 equals 9 over 12. 9 is more than 8, so 3 over 4 is greater.
steps: Use 40 as the common bottom number, because 8 times 5 equals 40.
Change 5 over 8. 5 over 8 equals 25 over 40.
Change 3 over 5. 3 over 5 equals 24 over 40.
25 over 40 is more than 24 over 40. The greater fraction is 5 over 8.

Q_CH07_022.q: 4 written as a fraction with denominator 3 is what?
hints: A whole number can be written as a fraction. Think about how many thirds make one whole.
One whole is 3 over 3. Work out how many thirds there are in 4 wholes.
Example: 5 written with denominator 2. One whole is 2 over 2, so 5 wholes are 5 times 2, which is 10 halves. So 5 equals 10 over 2.
steps: One whole is 3 thirds.
So 4 wholes are 12 thirds. 4 times 3 equals 12.
Check by dividing. So 4 is 12 over 3. 12 divided by 3 equals 4.

Q_CH07_023.q: What fraction of a day is 8 hours?
hints: To find what fraction one amount is of another, put the part over the whole. Both must be in the same unit.
How many hours are there in a day? Put 8 over that number, then simplify.
Example: what fraction of a day is 4 hours? A day has 24 hours, so it is 4 over 24. Divide the top and bottom by 4 to get 1 over 6.
steps: A day has 24 hours.
8 hours out of 24 hours is 8 over 24.
Divide the top and bottom by 8. 8 over 24 equals 1 over 3.
8 hours is one third of a day.

Q_CH07_023_V01.q: Rohan has 40 sweets and gives away 2 over 4 of them. How many sweets does Rohan give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 40 sweets into 4 equal groups first. Then think about how many of those groups Rohan gives away.
Example: 3 over 7 of 14 sweets. Share 14 into 7 equal groups: 14 divided by 7 equals 2. Take 3 of the groups: 2 times 3 equals 6. So 3 over 7 of 14 is 6 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 4, so share the 40 sweets into 4 equal groups. 40 divided by 4 equals 10.
The top number is 2, so Rohan gives away 2 of these groups. 10 times 2 equals 20.
Rohan gives away 20 sweets.

Q_CH07_024.q: A rope is 20 metres long. Three quarters of it is used. How many metres are used?
hints: To find a fraction of a length, share the length into equal parts and take some of them.
Divide 20 metres by 4 to find one quarter. Then think about how many quarters are used.
Example: a ribbon is 30 metres long and 3 over 5 of it is used. 30 divided by 5 equals 6, and 6 times 3 equals 18. So 18 metres is used.
steps: One quarter of 20 metres is 5 metres. 20 divided by 4 equals 5.
Three quarters is 3 of these parts. 5 times 3 equals 15.
15 metres of the rope is used.

Q_CH07_024_V01.q: Saanvi has 96 sweets and gives away 4 over 8 of them. How many sweets does Saanvi give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 96 sweets into 8 equal groups first. Then think about how many of those groups Saanvi gives away.
Example: 3 over 7 of 14 sweets. Share 14 into 7 equal groups: 14 divided by 7 equals 2. Take 3 of the groups: 2 times 3 equals 6. So 3 over 7 of 14 is 6 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 8, so share the 96 sweets into 8 equal groups. 96 divided by 8 equals 12.
The top number is 4, so Saanvi gives away 4 of these groups. 12 times 4 equals 48.
Saanvi gives away 48 sweets.

Q_CH07_024_V03.q: Aarav has 24 sweets and gives away three quarters of them. How many sweets does Aarav give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 24 sweets into 4 equal groups first. Then think about how many of those groups Aarav gives away.
Example: 5 over 8 of 56 sweets. Share 56 into 8 equal groups: 56 divided by 8 equals 7. Take 5 of the groups: 7 times 5 equals 35. So 5 over 8 of 56 is 35 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 4, so share the 24 sweets into 4 equal groups. 24 divided by 4 equals 6.
The top number is 3, so Aarav gives away 3 of these groups. 6 times 3 equals 18.
Aarav gives away 18 sweets.

Q_CH07_024_V07.q: Arjun has 18 sweets and gives away 3 over 6 of them. How many sweets does Arjun give away?
hints: Finding a fraction of a group means sharing it into equal groups. The bottom number tells you how many groups to make. The top number tells you how many groups to take.
Share the 18 sweets into 6 equal groups first. Then think about how many of those groups Arjun gives away.
Example: 5 over 8 of 56 sweets. Share 56 into 8 equal groups: 56 divided by 8 equals 7. Take 5 of the groups: 7 times 5 equals 35. So 5 over 8 of 56 is 35 sweets.
steps: The bottom number is 6, so share the 18 sweets into 6 equal groups. 18 divided by 6 equals 3.
The top number is 3, so Arjun gives away 3 of these groups. 3 times 3 equals 9.
Arjun gives away 9 sweets.

Q_CH07_025.q: I am a fraction. My numerator is 3 less than my denominator. I am equivalent to 4 over 7. What am I?
hints: The fraction must pass two tests at once. Check each choice against both clues.
First test: take the numerator away from the denominator and keep only the fractions where the answer is 3. Then check which of those is equal to 4 over 7.

Similar example: my numerator is 2 less than my denominator and I am equal to 3 over 5. Try 6 over 10: it equals 3 over 5, but 10 minus 6 equals 4. Try 5 over 7: 7 minus 5 equals 2, but it is not equal to 3 over 5. Try 3 over 5: 5 minus 3 equals 2 and it is 3 over 5 itself, so it passes both tests.
steps: Clue 1: the numerator is 3 less than the denominator. Check each fraction. 7 minus 4 equals 3, 11 minus 8 equals 3, 21 minus 12 equals 9, 14 minus 8 equals 6.
Only 4 over 7 and 8 over 11 pass the first clue.
Clue 2: the fraction is equal to 4 over 7. Doubling 4 over 7 gives 8 over 14, so 8 over 11 is not equal to 4 over 7. 4 times 2, all over 7 times 2, equals 8 over 14.
4 over 7 is equal to itself, and 7 minus 4 equals 3. So the fraction is 4 over 7.

hints: This sum has a subtraction, a multiplication and an addition all together. Think about which of the three has to be done first, before you go from left to right.
Work out 3 times 8 first and put that number in its place. Then do the subtraction and the addition in order from left to right.

Here is a similar one: 30 minus 4 times 5 plus 6. Multiply first: 4 times 5 equals 20. Now the sum reads 30 minus 20 plus 6. Going from left to right, 30 minus 20 equals 10, and then 10 plus 6 equals 16.
steps: Multiplication is done before subtraction and addition, so start with 3 times 8, which is 24.
Now the sum reads 50 minus 24 plus 2. Go from left to right and subtract first: 50 minus 24 equals 26.
Then add the 2: 26 plus 2 equals 28. The answer is 28.

hints: This sum has a subtraction, a multiplication and an addition all together. Think about which of the three has to be done first, before you go from left to right.

Here is a similar one: 50 minus 3 times 9 plus 2. Multiply first: 3 times 9 equals 27. Now the sum reads 50 minus 27 plus 2. Going from left to right, 50 minus 27 equals 23, and then 23 plus 2 equals 25.

Now the sum reads 29 minus 21 plus 8. Go from left to right and subtract first: 29 minus 21 equals 8.
Then add the 8: 8 plus 8 equals 16. The answer is 16.

Q_CH09_002.q: What is open bracket, 15 plus 5, close bracket, times 3?
hints: This sum has a bracket and a multiplication. Think about which part must always be done first.
Add the two numbers inside the bracket first. Only then multiply by the number outside.
Here is a similar one: open bracket, 7 plus 2, close bracket, times 4. The bracket is 7 plus 2, which is 9. Then 9 times 4 equals 36.
steps: The bracket is always done first: 15 plus 5 equals 20.
Now multiply by the 3 outside the bracket: 20 times 3 equals 60. The answer is 60.

hints: This sum has a division and an addition. Think about which of the two is done first.
Work out 36 divided by 6 first. After that, add the 14.
Here is a similar one: 48 divided by 8 plus 11. First 48 divided by 8 equals 6. Then 6 plus 11 equals 17.
steps: Division is done before addition, so start with 36 divided by 6, which is 6.
Now add the 14: 6 plus 14 equals 20. The answer is 20.

hints: This is a multiplication. It means equal groups added together.
Think of 2 groups of 4. Add 4 plus 4.
Here is a similar one: 2 times 6 means 2 groups of 6. 6 plus 6 equals 12, so 2 times 6 equals 12.
steps: 2 times 4 means 2 groups of 4. Add them up. 4 plus 4 equals 8.
2 times 4 equals 8.

Q_CH09_004.q: What is 48 divided by open bracket, 4 plus 4, close bracket, times 2?
hints: There is a bracket, a division and a multiplication. The bracket comes first, and then division and multiplication are done in order from left to right.
Add the numbers inside the bracket first. Then divide 48 by that number before you do any multiplying.
Here is a similar one: 36 divided by open bracket, 2 plus 4, close bracket, times 3. The bracket is 2 plus 4, which is 6. Then 36 divided by 6 equals 6, and 6 times 3 equals 18.
steps: Do the bracket first: 4 plus 4 equals 8.
Now the sum reads 48 divided by 8 times 2. Division and multiplication go from left to right, so divide first: 48 divided by 8 equals 6.
Then multiply: 6 times 2 equals 12. The answer is 12.

hints: This sum has a subtraction, a multiplication and an addition all together. Think about which of the three has to be done first, before you go from left to right.
Work out 7 times 2 first and put that number in its place. Then do the subtraction and the addition in order from left to right.

Here is a similar one: 30 minus 4 times 5 plus 6. Multiply first: 4 times 5 equals 20. Now the sum reads 30 minus 20 plus 6. Going from left to right, 30 minus 20 equals 10, and then 10 plus 6 equals 16.
steps: Multiplication is done before subtraction and addition, so start with 7 times 2, which is 14.
Now the sum reads 23 minus 14 plus 10. Go from left to right and subtract first: 23 minus 14 equals 9.
Then add the 10: 9 plus 10 equals 19. The answer is 19.

hints: This sum has a subtraction, a multiplication and an addition all together. Think about which of the three has to be done first, before you go from left to right.
Work out 8 times 3 first and put that number in its place. Then do the subtraction and the addition in order from left to right.

Here is a similar one: 30 minus 4 times 5 plus 6. Multiply first: 4 times 5 equals 20. Now the sum reads 30 minus 20 plus 6. Going from left to right, 30 minus 20 equals 10, and then 10 plus 6 equals 16.
steps: Multiplication is done before subtraction and addition, so start with 8 times 3, which is 24.
Now the sum reads 36 minus 24 plus 9. Go from left to right and subtract first: 36 minus 24 equals 12.
Then add the 9: 12 plus 9 equals 21. The answer is 21.

Q_CH09_005.q: What is open square bracket, 25 minus open curly bracket, 10 minus open bracket, 3 plus 2, close bracket, close curly bracket, close square bracket?
hints: There are three kinds of bracket here, one inside another. Start with the innermost bracket and work your way outwards.
Work out the round bracket, 3 plus 2, first. Then use that number inside the curly bracket.

Here is a similar one: open square bracket, 30 minus open curly bracket, 12 minus open bracket, 4 plus 1, close bracket, close curly bracket, close square bracket. First 4 plus 1 equals 5. Then 12 minus 5 equals 7. Last, 30 minus 7 equals 23.
