steps: Each number is a counting number multiplied by itself: 1 times 1 equals 1, 2 times 2 equals 4, 3 times 3 equals 9, 4 times 4 equals 16 and 5 times 5 equals 25.
The next one uses 6. 6 times 6 is 36, so the next number is 36.

hints: Look at the jumps between the numbers. If the jumps are not all the same, look for a pattern in the jumps themselves.
Work out the jumps from 1 to 3, from 3 to 6, from 6 to 10 and so on. See how much each jump grows by.
Here is a similar one: 4, 6, 9, 13, 18. The jumps are 2, 3, 4 and 5, going up by 1. The next jump is 6, so the next number is 18 plus 6, which is 24.
steps: Find the jumps: 3 minus 1 equals 2, 6 minus 3 equals 3, 10 minus 6 equals 4, 15 minus 10 equals 5 and 21 minus 15 equals 6.
The jumps go up by 1 each time, so the next jump is 7. 6 plus 1 equals 7.
Add 7 to the last number. The next number is 28. 21 plus 7 equals 28.

Q_CH16_017.q: What is the next term: 2, 5, 14, 41, blank?
hints: Look at the jumps between the terms. They are not steady, so see how each jump is made from the jump before it.
Work out the three jumps: from 2 to 5, from 5 to 14 and from 14 to 41. Ask yourself how many times bigger each jump is than the last.
Here is a similar one: 1, 3, 7, 15. The jumps are 2, 4 and 8, each double the one before. The next jump is 16, so the next term is 15 plus 16, which is 31.
steps: Find the jumps: 5 minus 2 equals 3, 14 minus 5 equals 9 and 41 minus 14 equals 27.
The jumps do not grow by adding. Each jump is 3 times the one before: 3 times 3 equals 9 and 9 times 3 equals 27. So the next jump is 81. 27 times 3 equals 81.
Add 81 to the last term to get 122. 41 plus 81 equals 122.
You can check another way. Each term is 3 times the one before, take away 1. 41 times 3 equals 123 and 123 minus 1 equals 122, so the next term is 122.

hints: The numbers grow faster and faster, so look at multiplying. See what each term is multiplied by to get the next one, and whether that multiplier changes.
Work out what 1 is multiplied by to give 2, then what 2 is multiplied by to give 6, then 6 to give 24. Look at those multipliers in order.
Here is a similar one: 4, 8, 24, 96. Here 4 times 2 equals 8, 8 times 3 equals 24 and 24 times 4 equals 96. The multiplier goes up by 1 each time, so the next term is 96 times 5, which is 480.
steps: See what each term is multiplied by to get the next: 1 times 2 equals 2, 2 times 3 equals 6, 6 times 4 equals 24 and 24 times 5 equals 120.
The multiplier goes up by 1 each time: 2, 3, 4, 5. The next multiplier is 6.
Multiply the last term by 6. The next term is 720. 120 times 6 equals 720.

Q_CH16_019.q: If A equals 1, B equals 2, C equals 3, and so on, what is the sum of the letters in the word MATH?
hints: Each letter stands for its place in the alphabet. Change every letter of the word into its number, then add the numbers.
Count along the alphabet to find the numbers for M, A, T and H. It helps to remember that J is 10 and T is 20.
Similar example: for the word dig, D is 4, I is 9 and G is 7. The sum of the letters is 4 plus 9 plus 7 equals 20.
steps: Find each letter's place in the alphabet. M is the 13th letter, A is the 1st, T is the 20th and H is the 8th.
Add the four numbers. 13 plus 1 plus 20 plus 8 equals 42.
The sum of the letters in MATH is 42.

hints: The jumps here are not steady. Look at how each number is linked to the two numbers just before it.
Add the first two numbers, 2 and 3, and compare the total with the third number. Then try the same with 3 and 5.
Here is a similar one: 1, 4, 5, 9, 14. Each number is the sum of the two before it: 1 plus 4 equals 5, 4 plus 5 equals 9 and 5 plus 9 equals 14. The next number is 9 plus 14, which is 23.
steps: Each number is the sum of the two before it: 2 plus 3 equals 5, 3 plus 5 equals 8, 5 plus 8 equals 13 and 8 plus 13 equals 21.
Add the last two numbers. The missing number is 34. 13 plus 21 equals 34.

hints: This sum mixes take away, times and add. The order you do them in matters.
Do the multiplication first: work out 6 times 3. After that, go from left to right.
Here is a similar one: 20 minus 2 times 5 plus 4. Multiply first: 2 times 5 equals 10. Then left to right: 20 minus 10 equals 10, and 10 plus 4 equals 14.
steps: Multiply first. 6 times 3 equals 18.
Now work from left to right. Take away the 18. 29 minus 18 equals 11.
Then add the 5. So the answer is 16, because 11 plus 5 equals 16.

hints: This sum mixes take away, times and add. The order you do them in matters.
Do the multiplication first: work out 3 times 9. After that, go from left to right.
Here is a similar one: 20 minus 2 times 5 plus 4. Multiply first: 2 times 5 equals 10. Then left to right: 20 minus 10 equals 10, and 10 plus 4 equals 14.
steps: Multiply first. 3 times 9 equals 27.
Now work from left to right. Take away the 27. 46 minus 27 equals 19.
Then add the 12. So the answer is 31, because 19 plus 12 equals 31.

hints: Find the differences: 3, 5, 7, 11, 9. Most differences are odd numbers increasing by 2.
Expected differences: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. The actual sequence should be: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37.
28 should be 26. So 28 is the number that doesn't belong!
steps: Differences: 3, 5, 7, 11, 9. The pattern breaks!
Expected: plus 3, plus 5, plus 7, plus 9, plus 11. Correct sequence: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37.
28 doesn't belong. It should be 26.

hints: The numbers grow faster and faster, so adding the same amount will not fit. See what each term is multiplied by to get the next one.
Compare 4 and 12, then 12 and 36. Ask yourself how many times bigger each term is than the one before.
Here is a similar one: 2, 10, 50, 250. Each term is 5 times the one before. So the next term is 250 times 5, which is 1250.
steps: See how each term is made from the one before: 4 times 3 equals 12, 12 times 3 equals 36 and 36 times 3 equals 108.
Each term is 3 times the one before. Multiply 108 by 3 to find that the next term is 324.

Q_CH16_023.q: The sequence 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42 follows the pattern n times, open bracket, n plus 1, close bracket. What is the 10th term?
hints: The rule is given to you: each term is its position number multiplied by the next counting number. You only need to use the rule for the right position.
Check the rule on a term you know. The 3rd term is 3 times 4, which is 12. Now decide which two numbers to multiply for the 10th term.
Here is a similar one. With the same rule, the 7th term is 7 times the next counting number, which is 8. 7 times 8 equals 56, so the 7th term is 56.
steps: The rule says the term in position n is n times the number just after n. Check it: the 1st term is 1 times 2, which is 2, and the 2nd term is 2 times 3, which is 6.
For the 10th term, n is 10 and the number just after it is 11. 10 plus 1 equals 11.
Multiply 10 by 11. The 10th term is 110. 10 times 11 equals 110.

hints: Find the ratio: 243 divided by 729 equals one third. 81 divided by 243 equals one third. Each term is divided by 3!
These are powers of 3: 3 to the power six equals 729, 3 to the power five equals 243, 3 to the power four equals 81, 3 cubed equals 27, 3 squared equals 9.
Next: 3 to the power one equals 3.
steps: Pattern: each term, divided by 3, equals the next term. 729 divided by 3 equals 243, 243 divided by 3 equals 81, and so on.
Or: 3 to the power six, 3 to the power five, 3 to the power four, 3 cubed, 3 squared, 3 to the power one.
The next one is 3 to the power one, which is 3.

hints: This looks like two patterns woven together. Try reading every other number, and then the numbers in between.
Write down the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th numbers on one line. Write the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th numbers on another line and compare the two lines.
Here is a similar one: 1, 2, 2, 4, 3, 6, 4. The 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th numbers are 1, 2, 3 and 4. The number after each of them is its double: 2, 4, 6. So after the 4 comes its double, 8.
steps: Two patterns are woven together. Take every other number, starting from the first: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. These are the counting numbers.
Now take the numbers in between: 1, 4, 9, 16. Each one is the number just before it multiplied by itself: 2 times 2 equals 4, 3 times 3 equals 9 and 4 times 4 equals 16.
The gap comes straight after 5, so it is 5 multiplied by itself. The next term is 25.

Q_CH17_001.q: Which of the following is a leap year?
hints: A leap year is a year that divides exactly by 4. Years that end in 00 are special: they are leap years only if they divide exactly by 400.
Sort the four years into two groups: those that end in 00 and those that do not. Test the 00 years with 400 and the others with 4.

Here is a similar one. Is 2016 a leap year? 2016 divided by 4 equals 504 with nothing left over, and it does not end in 00, so 2016 is a leap year. But 1800 ends in 00 and does not divide exactly by 400, so 1800 is not a leap year.
steps: A year is a leap year if it divides exactly by 4. Years ending in 00 must divide exactly by 400 instead.
2023 is an odd number, so it does not divide exactly by 4. It is not a leap year.
2100 and 1900 end in 00, and neither divides exactly by 400. So they are not leap years, even though they divide by 4. This is the trap.
2024 divides exactly by 4 and does not end in 00. So the leap year is 2024. 2024 divided by 4 equals 506.

Q_CH17_002.q: How many days are there from 1st March to 1st May, including both dates?
hints: Count the days month by month. Remember how many days each month has, and notice that both the first date and the last date are to be counted.
Start with March: count every day from the 1st to the 31st. Then think about how many days April has, and what is still left to count after April.
Here is a similar one. How many days are there from 1 April to 10 May, counting both dates? April has 30 days, and then there are 10 days in May. 30 plus 10 equals 40, so there are 40 days.
steps: Count all of March. From the 1st to the 31st is 31 days.
Count all of April, which has 30 days.
Then count 1 May itself, because both dates are included. That is 1 more day.
Add the three parts. There are 62 days. 31 plus 30 plus 1 equals 62.

Q_CH17_003.q: If 1st January 2023 was a Sunday, what day was 1st January 2024?
hints: From 1 January of one year to 1 January of the next is one whole year. Find how many days that is, then see how many are left over after full weeks.
Decide whether 2023 is a leap year by checking if it divides exactly by 4. That tells you how many days pass.
Here is a similar one. 1 January 2021 was a Friday. 2021 is not a leap year, so 365 days pass, which is 52 weeks and 1 day. The day moves on by 1, so 1 January 2022 was a Saturday.
steps: From 1 January 2023 to 1 January 2024 is the whole of 2023. 2023 is not a leap year, so that is 365 days.
52 weeks is 52 times 7 equals 364 days. So 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day.
After 52 full weeks it is Sunday again. One more day makes it Monday, so 1st January 2024 was a Monday.

Q_CH17_004.q: If 1st January 2024 was a Monday, what day was 1st January 2025?
hints: 2024 is a leap year, 366 days. How many extra days beyond complete weeks?
366 divided by 7 equals 52 weeks and 2 extra days.
2 extra days: Monday plus 2 is Wednesday.
steps: 2024 is a leap year: 366 days. 366 divided by 7 equals 52 weeks plus 2 days.
2 extra days: Monday plus 2 is Wednesday
1st January 2025 is Wednesday.

Q_CH17_005.q: Republic Day 1993 was on Tuesday. On which day did it fall in 1997?
hints: Count odd days from 1993 to 1997. Normal year equals 1 odd day. Leap year equals 2 odd days.
1993: 1 day, 1994: 1 day, 1995: 1 day, 1996: 2 days, leap! Total equals 5 odd days.
Tuesday plus 5 is Sunday.
steps: Count from 26 January 1993 to 26 January 1997: 4 years.
Odd days: 1 plus 1 plus 1 plus 2 equals 5
Tuesday plus 5 days is Sunday
Republic Day 1997 was Sunday.

Q_CH17_006.q: In 2007, Republic Day fell on Friday. On what day was it celebrated in 2008?
hints: Count the days from one Republic Day to the next, then see how many are left over after full weeks. Check whether a 29 February falls between the two dates.
Republic Day is 26 January. 2008 is a leap year, but its 29 February comes after 26 January. So decide how many days there are from 26 January 2007 to 26 January 2008.
Here is a similar one. 15 August 2013 was a Thursday. No 29 February lies between that day and 15 August 2014, so 365 days pass. That is 52 weeks and 1 day, so the day moves on by 1, to Friday.
steps: Republic Day is 26 January. Between 26 January 2007 and 26 January 2008 there is no 29 February, because the leap day of 2008 comes later, in February.
So 365 days pass. 52 weeks is 364 days, so that is 52 weeks and 1 day. 365 minus 364 equals 1.
The day moves on by 1, from Friday to Saturday. In 2008, Republic Day was celebrated on a Saturday.

Q_CH17_007.q: If 14th February 1992 was a Friday, what day did 13th February 1993 fall on?
hints: 1992 is a leap year! From 14 February 1992 to 14 February 1993 is 366 days, because it crosses 29 February 1992.
366 divided by 7 equals 52 weeks plus 2 days. So 14 February 1993 is Friday plus 2, which is Sunday.
But we want 13 February, one day before 14 February. Sunday minus 1 is Saturday.
steps: 1992 is a leap year. 14 February 1992 to 14 February 1993 equals 366 days.
14 February 1993 is Friday plus 2, which is Sunday
13 February 1993 is Sunday minus 1, which is Saturday
13 February 1993 was Saturday.

Q_CH17_008.q: In a certain year, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday occurred 5 times each in the month of July. Which date fell on a Sunday?
hints: A month of 31 days is 4 full weeks and 3 extra days. The days that come 5 times are the days that fall on the 1st, 2nd and 3rd.
Wednesday, Thursday and Friday come 5 times so decide which of them falls on 1 July. Then count forward to the first Sunday.

Here is a similar one. In a month of 30 days, Monday and Tuesday come 5 times. The two extra days, the 29th and 30th, match the 1st and 2nd, so the 1st is a Monday. The first Sunday is then the 7th, and the other Sundays are the 14th, 21st and 28th.
steps: July has 31 days, which is 4 weeks and 3 days. The three extra days, the 29th, 30th and 31st, fall on the same days as the 1st, 2nd and 3rd. 31 minus 28 equals 3.
The days that come 5 times are Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. So 1 July is a Wednesday, 2 July a Thursday and 3 July a Friday. Seeing this is the key to the question.
Then 4 July is a Saturday and 5 July is the first Sunday.
Add 7 each time to find the other Sundays: the 12th, the 19th and the 26th. The date that fell on a Sunday is 26th July. 19 plus 7 equals 26.

Q_CH17_009.q: Gandhi Jayanti, 2nd October, was celebrated on Wednesday. On which day did Children's Day, 14th November, fall in the same year?
hints: Count the days from 2nd October to 14th November.
October remaining: 31 minus 2 equals 29 days. November: 14 days. Total equals 29 plus 14, which is 43 days.
43 divided by 7 equals 6 weeks plus 1 day. Wednesday plus 1 is Thursday.
steps: Days from 2 October to 14 November: 29 in October, plus 14 in November equals 43
43 divided by 7 equals 6 weeks plus 1 day
Wednesday plus 1 is Thursday

Q_CH17_010.q: In 2020, Republic Day, 26 January, fell on Sunday. On which day was Independence Day, 15 August, celebrated that year?
hints: Count days from 26 January to 15 August. 2020 is a leap year, February equals 29 days.
January: 5, February: 29, March: 31, April: 30, May: 31, June: 30, July: 31, August: 15. Total equals 5 plus 29 plus 31 plus 30 plus 31 plus 30 plus 31 plus 15, which is 202.
202 divided by 7 equals 28 weeks plus 6 days. Sunday plus 6 is Saturday.
steps: Days: 5 in January, plus 29 in February, plus 31 in March, plus 30 in April, plus 31 in May, plus 30 in June, plus 31 in July, plus 15 in August
Total equals 202 days
Sunday plus 6 is Saturday

Q_CH17_011.q: How many minutes are there in 3 hours 45 minutes?
hints: Hours and minutes are different units. Change the hours into minutes first, then put all the minutes together.
One hour is 60 minutes. Work out how many minutes there are in 3 hours.
Here is a similar one. How many minutes are in 2 hours 20 minutes? 2 hours is 2 times 60 equals 120 minutes. Add the 20 minutes: 120 plus 20 equals 140 minutes.
steps: One hour is 60 minutes, so 3 hours is 180 minutes. 3 times 60 equals 180.
Add the extra 45 minutes. There are 225 minutes in 3 hours 45 minutes. 180 plus 45 equals 225.

Q_CH17_012.q: A movie starts at 2 40 p m and ends at 5 10 p m. How long is the movie?
hints: To find how long something lasts, count up from the start time to the end time. Counting up in easy jumps is safer than subtracting.
Start at 2 40 p m and jump to the next full hour, 3:00 p m. Note how many minutes that jump is, then carry on to 5 10 p m.

Here is a similar one. A class starts at 9 50 a m and ends at 12 15 p m. From 9 50 to 10:00 is 10 minutes, from 10:00 to 12:00 is 2 hours, and from 12:00 to 12 15 is 15 minutes. That is 2 hours and 10 plus 15 equals 25 minutes.
steps: Count up from 2 40 p m in easy jumps. From 2 40 to 3:00 is 20 minutes.
From 3:00 to 5:00 is 2 hours.
From 5:00 to 5 10 is 10 minutes.
Put the jumps together: 2 hours, and 20 minutes plus 10 minutes. The movie is 2 hours 30 minutes long. 20 plus 10 equals 30.

Q_CH17_013.q: What is 3 45 p m in 24-hour format?
hints: In 24-hour time the hours do not start again after noon. They carry on counting past 12, all the way to 23.
For a p m time, add 12 to the hours and leave the minutes as they are. Do that with the 3 in 3 45 p m.
Here is a similar one. Write 7 20 p m in 24-hour time. For a p m time, add 12 to the hours: 7 plus 12 equals 19. The minutes stay the same, so it is 19 20.
steps: In 24-hour time the hours carry on counting after 12 noon. For a p m time, add 12 to the hours.
Add 12 to the 3 hours to get hour 15. 3 plus 12 equals 15.
The minutes stay the same. So 3 45 p m is 15 45.

Q_CH17_014.q: How many odd days are there in 400 years?
hints: Odd days are the days left over after you take out all the full weeks. Count the odd days that the ordinary years and the leap years give, then take out full weeks again.
An ordinary year has 1 odd day and a leap year has 2. First find how many leap years there are in 400 years, remembering that a year ending in 00 is a leap year only if it divides exactly by 400.

Here is a similar one. How many odd days are there in 5 years, if one of them is a leap year? The four ordinary years give 4 odd days and the leap year gives 2. 4 plus 2 equals 6, which is less than a full week, so there are 6 odd days.
steps: An ordinary year is 52 weeks and 1 day, so it has 1 odd day. A leap year is 52 weeks and 2 days, so it has 2 odd days.
In 400 years, every 4th year makes 100 years. Three of the four years ending in 00 are not leap years, so there are 97 leap years and 303 ordinary years. 100 minus 3 equals 97.
The ordinary years give 303 odd days and the leap years give 97 times 2 equals 194 odd days. Together that is 497 days.
497 days is exactly 71 weeks, with nothing left over. So there are 0 odd days in 400 years. 497 divided by 7 equals 71.

Q_CH17_015.q: A Cricket World Cup began on 17th March, Wednesday. The final match was on the second Sunday in May. On what date was the final?
hints: First find what day May 1st falls on. From 17 March, Wednesday, to 1 May: 14 in March, plus 30 in April, plus 1 equals 45 days.
45 divided by 7 equals 6 weeks plus 3 days. Wednesday plus 3 is Saturday. So 1 May is Saturday.
If 1 May is Saturday, then 2 May is Sunday, the 1st Sunday. 9 May is Sunday, the 2nd Sunday.
steps: Days from 17 March to 1 May: 14 in March, plus 30 in April, plus 1 in May equals 45
45 divided by 7 equals 6 remainder 3. Wednesday plus 3 is Saturday. 1 May is Saturday.
Sundays in May: 2nd, 9th, 16th, and so on. The 2nd Sunday is 9th May.

Q_CH17_016.q: In 2003, April Fools' Day, 1st April, was on Tuesday. On which day was it celebrated in 2004?
hints: This is a calendar problem. The same date moves forward by a day or two of the week each year, so think about how many days lie between the two dates and whether a 29th of February falls between them.
Check whether 2004 is a leap year and whether its February comes before 1st April 2004. Then find how many days are left over after full weeks from 1st April 2003 to 1st April 2004.

Here is a similar problem. 15th August 2015 was a Saturday. Between 15th August 2015 and 15th August 2016 there is a 29th of February, because 2016 is a leap year, so there are 366 days. 366 days make 52 weeks and 2 days left over. Two days after Saturday is Monday, so 15th August 2016 was a Monday.
steps: From 1st April 2003 to 1st April 2004 is one full year. The year 2004 is a leap year and its 29th of February comes before 1st April, so this stretch has 366 days.
A week has 7 days. 366 days make 52 full weeks with 2 days left over. 366 equals 52 times 7 plus 2.
Full weeks bring us back to the same day, so only the 2 extra days matter. This is the trap: an ordinary year moves the day forward by 1, but the leap day makes it 2.
Two days after Tuesday is Thursday. So in 2004 it was celebrated on Thursday.

Q_CH17_017.q: In 2019, New Year, 1 January, fell on a Tuesday. On which day was Christmas, 25 December, celebrated in the same year?
hints: Count days from 1 January to 25 December. That's 358 days. 365 minus 7 equals 358. Let's count properly.

30 in January, plus 28 in February, plus 31 in March, plus 30 in April, plus 31 in May, plus 30 in June, plus 31 in July, plus 31 in August, plus 30 in September, plus 31 in October, plus 30 in November, plus 25 in December equals 358
358 divided by 7 equals 51 weeks plus 1 day. Tuesday plus 1 is Wednesday.
steps: Days from 1 January to 25 December, 2019, not a leap year. 30 plus 28 plus 31 plus 30 plus 31 plus 30 plus 31 plus 31 plus 30 plus 31 plus 30 plus 25 equals 358.
358 divided by 7 equals 51 remainder 1
Tuesday plus 1 is Wednesday

Q_CH17_018.q: 9th April 1990 was a Monday. Which days occurred five times in that month?
hints: This is a calendar problem. Every month has four full weeks plus a few extra days, and only the days of the week that land on those extra days come five times.
April has 30 days. Start by finding which day of the week the 1st of April was, by counting back in sevens from the 9th.

Here is a similar problem. Suppose 12th July is a Friday. Seven days earlier, the 5th is also a Friday, so the 4th is Thursday, the 3rd is Wednesday, the 2nd is Tuesday and the 1st is Monday. July has 31 days, which is 4 weeks and 3 days, so the first three days of the month, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, come five times.
steps: Counting back 7 days from Monday the 9th gives Monday the 2nd. The day before that, the 1st of April, was a Sunday. 9 minus 7 equals 2.
April has 30 days. That is 4 full weeks and 2 days more. 30 equals 4 times 7 plus 2.
In 4 full weeks every day of the week comes 4 times. The 2 extra days are the 29th and 30th, which fall on the same days as the 1st and 2nd.
Sundays fall on 1, 8, 15, 22 and 29, and Mondays fall on 2, 9, 16, 23 and 30. So the days that occurred five times are Sunday and Monday.

Q_CH17_019.q: A train departs at 09:45 and the journey takes 4 hours 35 minutes. At what time does it arrive?
hints: Add the journey time to the starting time. Add the hours and the minutes separately, and remember that 60 minutes make 1 hour.
Start by adding the 4 hours to 09:45. Then add the 35 minutes, and watch what happens when the minutes go past 60.

Similar example: a bus leaves at 10 50 and takes 2 hours 25 minutes. 10 50 plus 2 hours is 12 50. Then 50 plus 25 equals 75 minutes, which is 1 hour 15 minutes. So the bus arrives at 13 15, which is 1 15 p m.
steps: Add the 4 hours first. 09:45 plus 4 hours is 13 45. 9 plus 4 equals 13.
Now add the minutes. 45 plus 35 equals 80.
80 minutes is 1 hour and 20 minutes, so carry 1 hour. 80 minus 60 equals 20.
13 hours plus 1 hour is 14 hours, so the time is 14 20. On the 12-hour clock, 14 20 is 2 20 p m. 14 minus 12 equals 2.

Q_CH17_020.q: How many days are there from 15th August to 2nd October, not counting 15th August?
hints: This is a counting-days problem that runs across three months. Split it into the days left in the first month, the whole of the middle month, and the days used in the last month.
August has 31 days. Since 15th August is not counted, first find how many days are left in August after the 15th.

Here is a similar problem: the days from 20th March to 5th May, not counting 20th March. March has 31 days, so 31 minus 20 equals 11 days are left in March. April has 30 days, and May gives 5 days. 11 plus 30 plus 5 equals 46 days.
steps: August has 31 days. Leaving out the 15th, we count the 16th to the 31st, which is 16 days.
September has 30 days, and all of them are counted.
In October we count the 1st and the 2nd, which is 2 days. Take care here: the 15th of August is left out, but the 2nd of October is counted.
Add the three parts: 16 plus 30 plus 2 equals 48. So there are 48 days.

Q_CH17_021.q: Teacher's Day, 5th September, 2016 was a Monday. On which day was Christmas celebrated that year?
hints: Count days from 5 September to 25 December: 25 in September, plus 31 in October, plus 30 in November, plus 25 in December equals 111.
111 divided by 7 equals 15 weeks plus 6 days.
Monday plus 6 is Sunday.
steps: 25 in September, plus 31 in October, plus 30 in November, plus 25 in December equals 111
111 divided by 7 equals 15 remainder 6
Monday plus 6 is Sunday

Q_CH17_022.q: Rahul celebrated his 5th birthday on 3rd August 2014 which was a Sunday. Which birthday will fall on Thursday?
hints: Each year the same date moves forward by 1 weekday, or by 2 when a 29th February falls in between. Follow the birthdays one year at a time.
Start with 3rd August 2015, the 6th birthday. Then check whether a leap day comes before 3rd August 2016.

Similar example: Asha's 4th birthday is on 10th September 2018, a Monday. Her 5th birthday in 2019 is a Tuesday. Before September 2020 comes 29th February 2020, so her 6th birthday is 2 days on, a Thursday. Her 7th birthday in 2021 is a Friday.
steps: The 6th birthday is on 3rd August 2015. No leap day comes in between, so it is 1 day on: a Monday.
The 7th birthday is on 3rd August 2016. We pass 29th February 2016, so it is 2 days on: a Wednesday.
The 8th birthday is on 3rd August 2017. It is 1 day on: a Thursday.
So the 8th birthday falls on a Thursday.

Q_CH17_023.q: How many seconds are there in 2 hours?
hints: This is a time conversion with two jumps: hours to minutes, then minutes to seconds. Remember how many of the smaller unit make one of the bigger unit each time.
Start by changing 2 hours into minutes. One hour has 60 minutes.
Here is a similar problem: how many seconds are there in 3 hours? 3 hours is 3 times 60 equals 180 minutes. 180 minutes is 180 times 60 equals 10800 seconds.
steps: One hour has 60 minutes, so 2 hours have 2 times 60 equals 120 minutes.
One minute has 60 seconds, so 120 minutes have 120 times 60 equals 7200 seconds.
So there are 7200 seconds in 2 hours.

Q_CH17_024.q: A normal year has how many odd days?
hints: A normal year has 365 days. Divide by 7 to find complete weeks and extra days.
365 divided by 7 equals 52 weeks plus 1 day.
That 1 extra day is called 1 'odd day.' It's why the same date shifts by 1 day each normal year.
steps: 365 divided by 7 equals 52 weeks plus 1 day
Odd days equals 1

Q_CH17_025.q: In the year 2000, Gandhi Jayanti, 2nd October, fell on Monday. In which year was it first celebrated on Sunday after 2000?
hints: This is a calendar problem. The same date moves forward one day of the week after an ordinary year, and two days when a 29th of February falls in between. Follow the date year by year.

Start from Monday in 2000 and find the day for 2nd October 2001. The leap day of 2000 came in February, before October, so check whether any 29th of February lies between October 2000 and October 2001.

Here is a similar problem. 5th July 2010 was a Monday, and we want the first later year when 5th July fell on a Friday. In 2011 it was Tuesday. In 2012 it was Thursday, because 29th February 2012 falls in between and moves it 2 days. In 2013 it was Friday. So the year is 2013.
steps: From one 2nd October to the next is usually 365 days, which is 52 weeks and 1 day, so the day moves forward by 1. 365 equals 52 times 7 plus 1.
The leap day of 2000 was in February, before October, so it does not count here. In 2001 the day was Tuesday, in 2002 Wednesday and in 2003 Thursday.
Between October 2003 and October 2004 comes 29th February 2004. That stretch has 366 days, so the day jumps 2 days, from Thursday to Saturday. This is the trap: Friday is skipped.
One more ordinary year moves Saturday on to Sunday. So it was first celebrated on Sunday in 2005.

Q_CH18_001.q: An angle that measures more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees is called:
hints: This question is about the names of angles. Each name goes with a size, so think about where this angle sits compared with 90 degrees and 180 degrees.

Picture the corner of a book, which is 90 degrees, and a flat straight line, which is 180 degrees. This angle is wider than the corner of the book but has not opened out flat. Which name belongs to an angle like that?
A similar example: an angle of 40 degrees is smaller than 90 degrees, the corner of a book. Angles smaller than 90 degrees are called acute, so a 40 degree angle is an acute angle.
steps: An angle smaller than 90 degrees is called acute, and an angle of exactly 90 degrees is called a right angle.
An angle bigger than 180 degrees is called a reflex angle.
That leaves the angles in between. An angle that measures more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees is called obtuse.

Q_CH18_002.q: An angle measuring 250 degrees is a:
hints: 250 degrees is more than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees.
Reflex angles are between 180 degrees and 360 degrees.
So 250 degrees is a reflex angle.
steps: 180 degrees is less than 250 degrees, which is less than 360 degrees.
This falls in the reflex angle range.

Q_CH18_003.q: Which instrument is used to measure an angle?
hints: This question is about the tools in a geometry box. Each tool has one main job, so think about what each one is used for.
Angles are measured in degrees. Think about which tool in the box has degrees, from 0 degrees to 180 degrees, marked around its curved edge.

A similar example: to measure how long a line is, we use a ruler, because a ruler has centimetres marked along its edge. In the same way, the tool for measuring an angle is the one with degrees marked on it.
steps: Angles are measured in degrees, so we need a tool with degrees marked on it.
A compass draws circles, a pair of dividers compares lengths, and a set square helps draw a few fixed angles.
The half-circle tool marked from 0 degrees to 180 degrees is the one used to measure an angle. It is the protractor.

Q_CH18_004.q: What is the complementary angle of 67 and a half degrees?
hints: This question is about complementary angles. Remember what two complementary angles add up to, and then find the missing part.
Two complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. So take 67 and a half degrees away from 90 degrees. It is easier to take away the 67 degrees first and the half degree after that.

A similar example: find the complementary angle of 34 and a half degrees. First 90 degrees minus 34 degrees equals 56 degrees. Then take away the extra half degree, which leaves 55 and a half degrees. So the complementary angle of 34 and a half degrees is 55 and a half degrees.
steps: Two complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. So we take 67 and a half degrees away from 90 degrees.
Take away the whole degrees first. 90 degrees take away 67 degrees leaves 23 degrees. 90 degrees minus 67 degrees equals 23 degrees.
Now take away the extra half of a degree. 23 degrees take away half a degree leaves 22 and a half degrees.
The complementary angle of 67 and a half degrees is 22 and a half degrees.

Q_CH18_004_V05.q: Two angles of a triangle are 75 degrees and 67 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: Every triangle's three angles make 180 degrees altogether. You know two of them, so the third is whatever is left over.
First add the two angles you know, 75 degrees and 67 degrees. Then think about how far that total is from 180 degrees.
Similar example: two angles of a triangle are 48 degrees and 62 degrees. 48 plus 62 equals 110, and 180 minus 110 equals 70. The third angle is 70 degrees.
steps: Add the two angles you know. 75 plus 67 equals 142.
All three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Take the total away from 180 degrees. The third angle is 38 degrees. 180 minus 142 equals 38.

Q_CH18_004_V09.q: Two angles of a triangle are 36 degrees and 74 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: This uses the angle sum of a triangle: the three angles together make 180 degrees. Find the part that is missing.
First add the two angles you know, 36 degrees and 74 degrees. Then think about how far that total is from 180 degrees.
Similar example: two angles of a triangle are 33 degrees and 57 degrees. 33 plus 57 equals 90, and 180 minus 90 equals 90. The third angle is 90 degrees.
steps: Add the two angles you know. 36 plus 74 equals 110.
All three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Take the total away from 180 degrees. The third angle is 70 degrees. 180 minus 110 equals 70.

Q_CH18_005.q: What is the supplementary angle of 55 degrees?
hints: This question is about supplementary angles. Remember what two supplementary angles add up to, and then find the missing part.
Two supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, a straight line. So take 55 degrees away from 180 degrees.

A similar example: find the supplementary angle of 70 degrees. Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, and 180 degrees minus 70 degrees, which is 110 degrees. So the supplementary angle of 70 degrees is 110 degrees.
steps: Two supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, like the two angles on a straight line.
Take 55 degrees away from 180 degrees to find the other angle. 180 degrees minus 55 degrees equals 125 degrees.
The supplementary angle of 55 degrees is 125 degrees.

Q_CH18_005_V08.q: What is the supplement of an angle of 10 degrees?
hints: This is about supplementary angles. Two angles are supplementary when together they make a straight line.
Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees. So take 10 degrees away from 180 degrees.
Similar example: the supplement of 70 degrees is 180 degrees minus 70 degrees, which is 110 degrees. Check: 70 degrees plus 110 degrees equals 180 degrees.
steps: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 180 degrees. 180 degrees minus 10 degrees equals 170 degrees.
Check by adding: 10 degrees plus 170 degrees equals 180 degrees. The supplement of 10 degrees is 170 degrees.

Q_CH18_006.q: If x plus 35 degrees equals 90 degrees, what is the supplement of x?
hints: This question has two parts. First find the angle x, and then find its supplement. Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees.
Start with x plus 35 degrees equals 90 degrees. Ask yourself what must be added to 35 degrees to make 90 degrees. That number is x, and you still need its supplement after that.

A similar example: if y plus 20 degrees equals 90 degrees, then y equals 90 degrees minus 20 degrees, which is 70 degrees. The supplement of y is what you add to 70 degrees to make 180 degrees, and 180 degrees minus 70 degrees, which is 110 degrees. So the supplement of y is 110 degrees.
steps: First find x. It is the angle that adds to 35 degrees to make 90 degrees, so take 35 degrees away from 90 degrees. That gives x equals 55 degrees.
The question asks for the supplement of x, not x itself. Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees.
Take 55 degrees away from 180 degrees. The supplement of x is 125 degrees. 180 degrees minus 55 degrees equals 125 degrees.

Q_CH18_007.q: The supplement of an angle is 125 degrees. What is its complement?
hints: This question uses two ideas together. A supplement is measured against 180 degrees and a complement is measured against 90 degrees. You need to find the angle itself first.
The angle and its supplement add up to 180 degrees. So take 125 degrees away from 180 degrees to find the angle. After that, find what must be added to the angle to make 90 degrees.

A similar example: the supplement of an angle is 110 degrees. The angle is 180 degrees minus 110 degrees, which is 70 degrees. Its complement is 90 degrees minus 70 degrees, which is 20 degrees. So the complement is 20 degrees.
steps: An angle and its supplement add up to 180 degrees. So the angle is 180 degrees take away 125 degrees, which is 55 degrees. 180 degrees minus 125 degrees equals 55 degrees.
An angle and its complement add up to 90 degrees. So take 55 degrees away from 90 degrees. 90 degrees minus 55 degrees equals 35 degrees.
The complement of the angle is 35 degrees.

Q_CH18_008.q: When two lines cross, how many pairs of vertically opposite angles are formed?
hints: This question is about the angles made when two straight lines cross, like the letter X. Vertically opposite angles are the ones that face each other across the crossing point.
Draw two lines crossing and number the angles 1, 2, 3 and 4 going round the point. Now match each angle with the one directly across from it, and count the matches.

A similar example: the same two crossing lines also make pairs of angles that sit side by side. Going round the point, these are angles 1 and 2, 2 and 3, 3 and 4, and 4 and 1, so there are 4 side by side pairs. Count the pairs that sit across from each other in the same careful way.
steps: Two crossing lines make 4 angles around the point where they cross. Number them 1, 2, 3 and 4 going round.
Angle 1 is directly across from angle 3, so they make one pair. Angle 2 is directly across from angle 4, so they make another pair.
Every angle is now in a pair. So 2 pairs of vertically opposite angles are formed. 4 divided by 2 equals 2.

Q_CH18_009.q: Two lines intersect. One of the angles is 70 degrees. What is the angle opposite to it?
hints: Vertically opposite angles are always...
Equal! The angle opposite to 70 degrees is also 70 degrees.
That's the key property: vertically opposite angles are equal.
steps: Vertically opposite angles are equal.
The angle opposite to 70 degrees is 70 degrees.

Q_CH18_009_V04.q: What is the supplement of an angle of 85 degrees?
hints: This is about supplementary angles. Two angles are supplementary when together they make a straight line.
Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees. So take 85 degrees away from 180 degrees.
Similar example: the supplement of 70 degrees is 180 degrees minus 70 degrees, which is 110 degrees. Check: 70 degrees plus 110 degrees equals 180 degrees.
steps: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 180 degrees. 180 degrees minus 85 degrees equals 95 degrees.
Check by adding: 85 degrees plus 95 degrees equals 180 degrees. The supplement of 85 degrees is 95 degrees.

Q_CH18_010.q: Two adjacent angles form a linear pair. If one angle is 65 degrees, what is the other?
hints: This question is about a linear pair. The two angles sit side by side on a straight line, so think about what they add up to together.
A straight line makes an angle of 180 degrees. The two angles share it, so take 65 degrees away from 180 degrees.
A similar example: two angles form a linear pair and one of them is 110 degrees. Together they make 180 degrees, so the other is 180 degrees minus 110 degrees, which is 70 degrees.
steps: The two angles of a linear pair sit on a straight line, so they add up to 180 degrees.
Take 65 degrees away from 180 degrees to find the other angle. 180 degrees minus 65 degrees equals 115 degrees.
The other angle is 115 degrees.

Q_CH18_011.q: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at 3 o'clock?
hints: This question is about the angle between the hands of a clock. The 12 numbers split the clock face into 12 equal gaps, so first think about how big one gap is.

A full turn is 360 degrees and the clock has 12 equal gaps, so each gap is 360 degrees divided by 12, which is 30 degrees. At 3 o'clock the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand points at 3. Count the gaps between them.
A similar example: at 5 o'clock the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand points at 5. That is 5 gaps, and each gap is 30 degrees, so the angle is 5 times 30 degrees, which is 150 degrees.
steps: The clock face is a full turn of 360 degrees, split into 12 equal gaps. Each gap is 30 degrees. 360 degrees divided by 12 equals 30 degrees.
At 3 o'clock the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand points at 3. There are 3 gaps between them.
Three gaps of 30 degrees make 90 degrees. The angle between the hands at 3 o'clock is 90 degrees. 3 times 30 degrees equals 90 degrees.

Q_CH18_012.q: Find the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at 9 30.
hints: This is a clock angle question with a catch. At half past the hour, the hour hand is no longer pointing exactly at a number, so think about where each hand really is.
At 9 30 the minute hand points at 6. The hour hand has moved halfway from 9 to 10. Count the gaps from 6 up to that halfway point, remembering that each full gap is 30 degrees.

A similar example: at 7 30 the minute hand points at 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 7 and 8. From 6 to 7 is 1 full gap, which is 30 degrees. Half a gap more is 15 degrees. So the angle is 30 degrees plus 15 degrees, which is 45 degrees.
steps: At 9 30 the minute hand points at 6. The hour hand does not point at 9. In half an hour it has moved halfway from 9 to 10.
Each gap between two numbers is 30 degrees. From 6 to 9 is 3 gaps, which is 90 degrees. 3 times 30 degrees equals 90 degrees.
The hour hand is half a gap past 9. Half of 30 degrees is 15 degrees.
Add the two parts together. The angle between the hands at 9 30 is 105 degrees. 90 degrees plus 15 degrees equals 105 degrees.

Q_CH18_012_V08.q: What is the supplement of an angle of 165 degrees?
hints: This is about supplementary angles. Two angles are supplementary when together they make a straight line.
Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees. So take 165 degrees away from 180 degrees.
Similar example: the supplement of 70 degrees is 180 degrees minus 70 degrees, which is 110 degrees. Check: 70 degrees plus 110 degrees equals 180 degrees.
steps: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 180 degrees. 180 degrees minus 165 degrees equals 15 degrees.
Check by adding: 165 degrees plus 15 degrees equals 180 degrees. The supplement of 165 degrees is 15 degrees.

Q_CH18_013.q: At which of these times will the angle between the clock hands be obtuse?
hints: This question joins two ideas, clock angles and the names of angles. An obtuse angle is more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees, so you need the angle at each time.
Each gap between two numbers on the clock is 30 degrees. Start with the o'clock times, where the hour hand points exactly at a number, and count the gaps between the two hands.

A similar example: at 5:00 the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand points at 5. That is 5 gaps, and 5 times 30 degrees equals 150 degrees. Since 150 degrees is between 90 degrees and 180 degrees, the angle at 5:00 is obtuse. Test each time in the list in the same way.
steps: Each gap between two numbers on a clock is 30 degrees. An obtuse angle is more than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees.
At 10:00 the hands are 2 gaps apart, which is 60 degrees. That is less than 90 degrees, so it is acute. 2 times 30 degrees equals 60 degrees.
At 6:00 the hands are 6 gaps apart, which is 180 degrees. That is a straight angle, not an obtuse one. 6 times 30 degrees equals 180 degrees.
At 3 30 the minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4. That is 2 and a half gaps, which is 75 degrees, so it is acute. 2 times 30 degrees, plus 15 degrees, equals 75 degrees.
At 4:00 the hands are 4 gaps apart, which is 120 degrees. That is between 90 degrees and 180 degrees, so the angle is obtuse at 4:00. 4 times 30 degrees equals 120 degrees.

Q_CH18_014.q: When will the hour hand and the minute hand form a straight angle, 180 degrees?
hints: This is a clock angle question. A straight angle means the two hands point in exactly opposite directions, so think carefully about where the hour hand really is at each time.
The hour hand points exactly at a number only at an o'clock time. At 3 45 and at 9 15 it has already moved away from its number. Check whether the hands are still exactly opposite at those times.

A similar example: at 3:00 the minute hand is on 12 and the hour hand is exactly on 3, so the angle is 3 times 30 degrees, which is 90 degrees. At 12 15 the minute hand is on 3, but the hour hand has crept a little past 12, so the angle is a little less than 90 degrees.
steps: At 6:00 the minute hand is on 12 and the hour hand is exactly on 6. They are 6 gaps apart, and each gap is 30 degrees, so the angle is 180 degrees. 6 times 30 degrees equals 180 degrees.
At 3 45 the minute hand is on 9, but the hour hand has moved most of the way from 3 to 4. The hands are not exactly opposite.
At 9 15 the minute hand is on 3, but the hour hand has moved a little past 9. The hands are not exactly opposite here either.
So the hands form a straight angle only at 6:00.

Q_CH18_014_V08.q: Two angles of a triangle are 34 degrees and 60 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: The three angles of a triangle always add up to 180 degrees. Two are given, so find what is left for the third.
First add the two angles you know, 34 degrees and 60 degrees. Then think about how far that total is from 180 degrees.
Similar example: two angles of a triangle are 25 degrees and 110 degrees. 25 plus 110 equals 135, and 180 minus 135 equals 45. The third angle is 45 degrees.
steps: Add the two angles you know. 34 plus 60 equals 94.
All three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Take the total away from 180 degrees. The third angle is 86 degrees. 180 minus 94 equals 86.

Q_CH18_014_V10.q: Two angles of a triangle are 63 degrees and 87 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: Every triangle's three angles make 180 degrees altogether. You know two of them, so the third is whatever is left over.
First add the two angles you know, 63 degrees and 87 degrees. Then think about how far that total is from 180 degrees.
Similar example: two angles of a triangle are 40 degrees and 65 degrees. 40 plus 65 equals 105, and 180 minus 105 equals 75. The third angle is 75 degrees.
steps: Add the two angles you know. 63 plus 87 equals 150.
All three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Take the total away from 180 degrees. The third angle is 30 degrees. 180 minus 150 equals 30.

Q_CH18_015.q: At which of these times is the angle between the clock hands the greatest?
hints: Work out the angle between the hands for each time, then compare. Remember that the hour hand keeps moving slowly as the minutes pass.
The clock face has 12 gaps of 30 degrees each. For each time, find where the minute hand points, find where the hour hand is, and count the gaps between them. Start with 9:00.
Similar example: at 3 30 the minute hand is on the 6. The hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4. From there to the 6 is 2 and a half gaps, and 2.5 times 30 degrees equals 75 degrees.
steps: The clock has 12 gaps between the numbers, and each gap is 30 degrees. 360 divided by 12 equals 30.
At 9:00 the hands are on 9 and 12, which is 3 gaps. 3 times 30 equals 90 degrees.
At 4 30 the minute hand is on 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 4 and 5. That is 1 and a half gaps. 1.5 times 30 equals 45 degrees.
At 12 15 the minute hand is on 3. The hour hand has moved a quarter of a gap past 12, so there are 2 and three-quarter gaps between them. 2.75 times 30 equals 82.5 degrees.
At 6 15 the minute hand is on 3. The hour hand is a quarter of a gap past 6, so there are 3 and a quarter gaps between them. 3.25 times 30 equals 97.5 degrees.
Compare 45 degrees, 97.5 degrees, 90 degrees and 82.5 degrees. The greatest angle is 97.5 degrees, at 6 15.

Q_CH18_016.q: At 1 o'clock, the angle between clock hands is 30 degrees. At what time will the angle be complementary to this?
hints: Complementary to 30 degrees means the angle should be 90 degrees minus 30 degrees, which is 60 degrees.
60 degrees is 2 spaces on the clock. Which time gives exactly 2 spaces?
At 2 o'clock, the hands are 2 spaces apart, which is 60 degrees.
steps: The complement of 30 degrees is 90 degrees minus 30 degrees, which is 60 degrees.
60 degrees is 2 spaces on the clock, which is 2 o'clock.
At 2 o'clock, the angle is 60 degrees.

Q_CH18_016_V01.q: What is the complement of an angle of 27 degrees?
hints: This is about complementary angles. Two angles are complementary when together they make a right angle.
Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. So take 27 degrees away from 90 degrees.
Similar example: the complement of 20 degrees is 90 degrees minus 20 degrees, which is 70 degrees. Check: 20 degrees plus 70 degrees equals 90 degrees.
steps: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 90 degrees. 90 degrees minus 27 degrees equals 63 degrees.
Check by adding: 27 degrees plus 63 degrees equals 90 degrees. The complement of 27 degrees is 63 degrees.

Q_CH18_016_V06.q: Two angles of a triangle are 27 degrees and 41 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: This uses the angle sum of a triangle: the three angles together make 180 degrees. Find the part that is missing.
First add the two angles you know, 27 degrees and 41 degrees. Then think about how far that total is from 180 degrees.
Similar example: two angles of a triangle are 35 degrees and 80 degrees. 35 plus 80 equals 115, and 180 minus 115 equals 65. The third angle is 65 degrees.
steps: Add the two angles you know. 27 plus 41 equals 68.
All three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Take the total away from 180 degrees. The third angle is 112 degrees. 180 minus 68 equals 112.

Q_CH18_016_V07.q: What is the complement of an angle of 85 degrees?
hints: This is about complementary angles. Two angles are complementary when together they make a right angle.
Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. So take 85 degrees away from 90 degrees.
Similar example: the complement of 20 degrees is 90 degrees minus 20 degrees, which is 70 degrees. Check: 20 degrees plus 70 degrees equals 90 degrees.
steps: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 90 degrees. 90 degrees minus 85 degrees equals 5 degrees.
Check by adding: 85 degrees plus 5 degrees equals 90 degrees. The complement of 85 degrees is 5 degrees.

Q_CH18_017.q: What is the angle between North-East and South directions?
hints: This question is about directions on a compass. The four main directions are a quarter turn apart, and the in-between directions sit exactly halfway.
North, East, South and West are 90 degrees apart. North-East is halfway between North and East. Go from North-East to East first, and then on from East to South.

A similar example: find the angle between North-East and North-West. From North-East to North is half of 90 degrees, which is 45 degrees. From North to North-West is another 45 degrees. So the angle is 45 degrees plus 45 degrees, which is 90 degrees.
steps: North, East, South and West are each 90 degrees apart. North-East is exactly halfway between North and East.
From North-East to East is half of 90 degrees, which is 45 degrees.
From East to South is one quarter turn, which is 90 degrees.
Add the two parts. The angle between North-East and South is 135 degrees. 45 degrees plus 90 degrees equals 135 degrees.

Q_CH18_018.q: How many degrees does the hour hand move in one hour?
hints: This question is about how fast the hour hand turns. Think about how long the hour hand takes to go once all the way round the clock.
The hour hand makes one full turn of 360 degrees in 12 hours. Share 360 degrees equally among the 12 hours.

A similar example: how far does the hour hand turn in 3 hours? It turns 360 degrees in 12 hours, and 3 hours is one quarter of 12 hours. One quarter of 360 degrees is 360 degrees divided by 4, which is 90 degrees. So it turns 90 degrees in 3 hours.
steps: The hour hand goes once round the clock in 12 hours. One full turn is 360 degrees.
Share 360 degrees equally among the 12 hours. 360 degrees divided by 12 equals 30 degrees.
The hour hand moves 30 degrees in one hour.

Q_CH18_018_V04.q: What is the complement of an angle of 8 degrees?
hints: This is about complementary angles. Two angles are complementary when together they make a right angle.
Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. So take 8 degrees away from 90 degrees.
Similar example: the complement of 20 degrees is 90 degrees minus 20 degrees, which is 70 degrees. Check: 20 degrees plus 70 degrees equals 90 degrees.
steps: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 90 degrees. 90 degrees minus 8 degrees equals 82 degrees.
Check by adding: 8 degrees plus 82 degrees equals 90 degrees. The complement of 8 degrees is 82 degrees.

Q_CH18_019.q: How many degrees does the minute hand move in 1 minute?
hints: This question is about how fast the minute hand turns. Think about how long the minute hand takes to go once all the way round the clock.
The minute hand makes one full turn of 360 degrees in 60 minutes. Share 360 degrees equally among the 60 minutes.

A similar example: how far does the minute hand turn in 15 minutes? It turns 360 degrees in 60 minutes, and 15 minutes is one quarter of that time. One quarter of 360 degrees is 360 degrees divided by 4, which is 90 degrees. So it turns 90 degrees in 15 minutes.
steps: The minute hand goes once round the clock in 60 minutes. One full turn is 360 degrees.
Share 360 degrees equally among the 60 minutes. 360 degrees divided by 60 equals 6 degrees.
The minute hand moves 6 degrees in 1 minute.

Q_CH18_020.q: Two complementary angles are in the ratio 2 is to 3. Find the smaller angle.
hints: This question joins complementary angles with a ratio. First decide what the two angles add up to, and then share that total in the ratio.
Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. The ratio 2 is to 3 means 2 equal parts and 3 equal parts, so there are 5 equal parts altogether. Find the size of one part first.

A similar example: two complementary angles are in the ratio 4 is to 5. There are 4 plus 5, which is 9 parts, so one part is 90 degrees divided by 9, which is 10 degrees. The smaller angle is 4 times 10 degrees, which is 40 degrees, and the larger is 5 times 10 degrees, which is 50 degrees.
steps: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. The ratio 2 is to 3 means there are 5 equal parts altogether. 2 plus 3 equals 5.
Find one part by sharing 90 degrees into 5 equal parts. 90 degrees divided by 5 equals 18 degrees.
The smaller angle has 2 of these parts. 2 times 18 degrees equals 36 degrees.
The larger angle is 3 times 18 degrees, which is 54 degrees, and 36 degrees plus 54 degrees, which is 90 degrees. So the smaller angle is 36 degrees.

Q_CH18_020_V07.q: What is the supplement of an angle of 118 degrees?
hints: This is about supplementary angles. Two angles are supplementary when together they make a straight line.
Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees. So take 118 degrees away from 180 degrees.
Similar example: the supplement of 70 degrees is 180 degrees minus 70 degrees, which is 110 degrees. Check: 70 degrees plus 110 degrees equals 180 degrees.
steps: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 180 degrees. 180 degrees minus 118 degrees equals 62 degrees.
Check by adding: 118 degrees plus 62 degrees equals 180 degrees. The supplement of 118 degrees is 62 degrees.

Q_CH18_021.q: Two supplementary angles differ by 40 degrees. Find the larger angle.
hints: This is a sum and difference question. You know what the two angles add up to and how far apart they are, and you need the bigger one.
Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees. Take the extra 40 degrees away from 180 degrees first. What is left is two equal shares, one for each angle.

A similar example: two supplementary angles differ by 30 degrees. Take away the extra, 180 degrees minus 30 degrees equals 150 degrees. Halve it to get the smaller angle, 150 degrees divided by 2 equals 75 degrees. The larger is 75 degrees plus 30 degrees, which is 105 degrees. Check: 105 degrees plus 75 degrees equals 180 degrees.
steps: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees. The larger angle is the smaller angle with 40 degrees extra.
Take the extra 40 degrees away from the total. What is left is two copies of the smaller angle. 180 degrees minus 40 degrees equals 140 degrees.
Halve 140 degrees to find the smaller angle. 140 degrees divided by two equals 70 degrees.
Add the extra 40 degrees back to get the larger angle. Check that 110 degrees plus 70 degrees equals 180 degrees. The larger angle is 110 degrees. 70 degrees plus 40 degrees equals 110 degrees.

Q_CH18_022.q: Three angles meeting at a point are 110 degrees, 85 degrees, and x degrees. Find x.
hints: This question is about angles that meet at a point. Together they go all the way round the point, so think about what a full turn measures.
Angles around a point add up to 360 degrees. Add the two angles you know, 110 degrees and 85 degrees, and then take that total away from 360 degrees.

A similar example: three angles meeting at a point are 120 degrees, 100 degrees and y degrees. The two known angles add up to 120 degrees plus 100 degrees, which is 220 degrees. So y equals 360 degrees minus 220 degrees, which is 140 degrees.
steps: The three angles go all the way round the point, so they add up to 360 degrees.
Add the two angles you know. 110 degrees plus 85 degrees equals 195 degrees.
Take this away from the full turn to find the third angle. 360 degrees minus 195 degrees equals 165 degrees.
So x is 165 degrees.

Q_CH18_022_V05.q: What is the complement of an angle of 55 degrees?
hints: This is about complementary angles. Two angles are complementary when together they make a right angle.
Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. So take 55 degrees away from 90 degrees.
Similar example: the complement of 20 degrees is 90 degrees minus 20 degrees, which is 70 degrees. Check: 20 degrees plus 70 degrees equals 90 degrees.
steps: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 90 degrees. 90 degrees minus 55 degrees equals 35 degrees.
Check by adding: 55 degrees plus 35 degrees equals 90 degrees. The complement of 55 degrees is 35 degrees.

Q_CH18_022_V07.q: Two angles of a triangle are 39 degrees and 79 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: The three angles of a triangle always add up to 180 degrees. Two are given, so find what is left for the third.
First add the two angles you know, 39 degrees and 79 degrees. Then think about how far that total is from 180 degrees.
Similar example: two angles of a triangle are 55 degrees and 45 degrees. 55 plus 45 equals 100, and 180 minus 100 equals 80. The third angle is 80 degrees.
steps: Add the two angles you know. 39 plus 79 equals 118.
All three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Take the total away from 180 degrees. The third angle is 62 degrees. 180 minus 118 equals 62.

Q_CH18_023.q: Angles on a straight line are x degrees, 2 x degrees, and 3 x degrees. Find x.
hints: This question is about angles on a straight line. Think about what they add up to, and how many equal shares of x there are altogether.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees. The angles are 1 lot of x, 2 lots of x and 3 lots of x. Count how many lots of x that is altogether.

A similar example: the angles on a straight line are y degrees and 4 y degrees. That is 1 plus 4, which is 5 lots of y, and they add up to 180 degrees. So y equals 180 degrees divided by 5, which is 36 degrees. Check: 36 degrees plus 144 degrees equals 180 degrees.
steps: Angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees.
The angles are 1 lot of x, 2 lots of x and 3 lots of x. That is 6 lots of x altogether. 1 plus 2 plus 3 equals 6.
Six lots of x make 180 degrees, so share 180 degrees into 6 equal parts. 180 degrees divided by 6 equals 30 degrees.
Check: the angles are 30 degrees, 60 degrees and 90 degrees, and they add up to 180 degrees. So x is 30 degrees. 30 degrees plus 60 degrees plus 90 degrees equals 180 degrees.

Q_CH18_024.q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 4 30?
hints: This is a clock angle question with a catch. At half past the hour, the hour hand is no longer pointing exactly at a number, so think about where each hand really is.
At 4 30 the minute hand points at 6. The hour hand has moved halfway from 4 to 5. Count the gaps from that halfway point to 6, remembering that each full gap is 30 degrees.

A similar example: at 1 30 the minute hand points at 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 1 and 2. From 2 to 6 is 4 full gaps, which is 4 times 30 degrees equals 120 degrees. Half a gap more is 15 degrees. So the angle is 120 degrees plus 15 degrees, which is 135 degrees.
steps: At 4 30 the minute hand points at 6. The hour hand does not point at 4. In half an hour it has moved halfway from 4 to 5.
Each gap between two numbers is 30 degrees. From 5 to 6 is 1 full gap, which is 30 degrees.
From the hour hand to 5 is half a gap. Half of 30 degrees is 15 degrees.
Add the two parts together. The angle between the hands at 4 30 is 45 degrees. 30 degrees plus 15 degrees equals 45 degrees.

Q_CH18_025.q: A person facing North turns clockwise through 225 degrees. Which direction is he now facing?
hints: Start at North, 0 degrees, and turn 225 degrees clockwise. North is 0 degrees, East is 90 degrees, South is 180 degrees, West is 270 degrees.
225 degrees is between South, at 180 degrees, and West, at 270 degrees. It's 45 degrees past South.
45 degrees past South, towards West, is South-West.
steps: On the compass, North is 0 degrees, East is 90 degrees, South is 180 degrees, West is 270 degrees. 225 degrees is between South and West.
225 degrees is 180 degrees plus 45 degrees. That is South, plus 45 degrees towards West.
The direction is South-West.

Q_CH19_001.q: Each angle of an equilateral triangle measures:
hints: This is about the angles of a triangle. In an equilateral triangle all three angles are equal, and the angles of any triangle add up to the same total.
The three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. Think about how to share 180 degrees equally among 3 angles.
Here is a similar problem. A square has four equal angles, and they add up to 360 degrees. Each angle is 360 divided by 4, which is 90 degrees.
steps: The three angles of any triangle add up to 180 degrees.
In an equilateral triangle all three angles are equal, so we share 180 degrees equally among 3 angles.
180 divided by 3 equals 60. So each angle measures 60 degrees.

Q_CH19_002.q: The perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side 7 centimetres is:
hints: This is a perimeter problem. Perimeter is the total distance around a shape, and an equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
All three sides are 7 centimetres long. Add the three sides together, or multiply the side by 3.
Here is a similar problem: an equilateral triangle with side 9 centimetres. Its three sides are all 9 centimetres, so the perimeter is 3 times 9, which is 27 centimetres.
steps: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides, so each side is 7 centimetres.
The perimeter is the sum of all the sides, 7 plus 7 plus 7, which is 3 times 7 equals 21. So the perimeter is 21 centimetres.

Q_CH19_002_V09.q: A rectangle is 8 centimetres long and 3 centimetres wide. What is its area?
hints: This asks for area, the space inside the rectangle. Think about how the length and the width work together to cover it.
The area of a rectangle is length times width. Set up 8 times 3 and work it out.
Here is a similar one: a rectangle 12 centimetres long and 5 centimetres wide. Area equals 12 times 5, which is 60 square centimetres.
steps: The area of a rectangle is length times width.
8 times 3 means 8 groups of 3. Add them up. 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 equals 24.
So the area is 24 square centimetres. 8 times 3 equals 24.

Q_CH19_003.q: Two angles of a triangle are 35 degrees and 65 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: This is a missing-angle problem. The three angles of any triangle always add up to the same total.
The three angles add up to 180 degrees. Start by adding the two angles you know, 35 degrees and 65 degrees.
Here is a similar problem. Two angles of a triangle are 50 degrees and 70 degrees. Together they make 50 plus 70, which is 120 degrees. The third angle is 180 minus 120, which is 60 degrees.
steps: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
The two known angles add up to 35 plus 65, which is 100 degrees.
The third angle is what is left: 180 minus 100 equals 80. So the third angle is 80 degrees.

Q_CH19_003_V06.q: Two angles of a triangle are 52 degrees and 59 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: Every triangle's three angles make 180 degrees altogether. You know two of them, so the third is whatever is left over.
First add the two angles you know, 52 degrees and 59 degrees. Then think about how far that total is from 180 degrees.
Similar example: two angles of a triangle are 20 degrees and 95 degrees. 20 plus 95 equals 115, and 180 minus 115 equals 65. The third angle is 65 degrees.
steps: Add the two angles you know. 52 plus 59 equals 111.
All three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Take the total away from 180 degrees. The third angle is 69 degrees. 180 minus 111 equals 69.

Q_CH19_003_V08.q: What is the complement of an angle of 43 degrees?
hints: This is about complementary angles. Two angles are complementary when together they make a right angle.
Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. So take 43 degrees away from 90 degrees.
Similar example: the complement of 20 degrees is 90 degrees minus 20 degrees, which is 70 degrees. Check: 20 degrees plus 70 degrees equals 90 degrees.
steps: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 90 degrees. 90 degrees minus 43 degrees equals 47 degrees.
Check by adding: 43 degrees plus 47 degrees equals 90 degrees. The complement of 43 degrees is 47 degrees.

Q_CH19_004.q: If two angles of a triangle are 28 degrees and 45 degrees, what type of triangle is it?
hints: This asks you to name a triangle by its angles. A triangle is acute-angled if all its angles are less than 90 degrees, right-angled if one angle is exactly 90 degrees, and obtuse-angled if one angle is more than 90 degrees. You need all three angles to decide.
The three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. First find the third angle by adding 28 degrees and 45 degrees and taking the sum away from 180 degrees.

Here is a similar problem. Two angles of a triangle are 60 degrees and 50 degrees. Together they make 110 degrees, so the third angle is 180 minus 110, which is 70 degrees. All three angles are less than 90 degrees, so that triangle is acute-angled.
steps: The two known angles add up to 28 plus 45, which is 73 degrees.
The three angles add up to 180 degrees, so the third angle is 180 minus 73, which is 107 degrees.
107 degrees is more than 90 degrees, so it is an obtuse angle.
A triangle with one obtuse angle is an obtuse-angled triangle.

Q_CH19_005.q: Which of the following can be the lengths of the sides of a triangle?
hints: This is about which three lengths can make a triangle. The two shorter sides together must be longer than the longest side, or they cannot meet.
For each set, add the two shorter lengths and compare the sum with the longest length. Start with 2 centimetres, 5 centimetres and 9 centimetres.

Here is a similar problem. Can 3 centimetres, 4 centimetres and 9 centimetres make a triangle? 3 plus 4 equals 7, which is less than 9, so they cannot. Can 4 centimetres, 7 centimetres and 10 centimetres make a triangle? 4 plus 7 equals 11, which is more than 10, so they can.
steps: Three lengths make a triangle only when the two shorter sides together are longer than the longest side.
For 2 centimetres, 5 centimetres and 9 centimetres: 2 plus 5 equals 7, which is less than 9, so the short sides cannot meet.
For 1 centimetre, 5 centimetres and 6 centimetres: 1 plus 5 equals 6, which is only equal to the longest side, so the short sides would lie flat along it.
For 6 centimetres, 8 centimetres and 12 centimetres: 6 plus 8 equals 14, which is more than 12. So the lengths that can make a triangle are 6 centimetres, 8 centimetres and 12 centimetres.

Q_CH19_006.q: Which of the following are the measures of the angles of an isosceles triangle?
hints: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, and so it also has two equal angles. Look for a set of angles with a matching pair.
Go through each set and see whether any angle appears twice. Start with 30 degrees, 60 degrees and 90 degrees.

Here is a similar problem. Which is isosceles: a triangle with angles 50 degrees, 60 degrees, 70 degrees or one with angles 40 degrees, 40 degrees, 100 degrees? The first has three different angles. The second has two angles of 40 degrees, and 40 plus 40 plus 100, which is 180, so the second one is isosceles.
steps: An isosceles triangle has two equal angles.
In 30 degrees, 60 degrees, 90 degrees, in 40 degrees, 120 degrees, 20 degrees and in 50 degrees, 90 degrees, 40 degrees, all three angles are different.
In the remaining set two angles are both 75 degrees, and the three angles add up to 180 degrees. 30 plus 75 plus 75 equals 180.
So the angles of an isosceles triangle are 30 degrees, 75 degrees, 75 degrees.

Q_CH19_006_V09.q: Two angles of a triangle are 61 degrees and 26 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: This uses the angle sum of a triangle: the three angles together make 180 degrees. Find the part that is missing.
First add the two angles you know, 61 degrees and 26 degrees. Then think about how far that total is from 180 degrees.
Similar example: two angles of a triangle are 48 degrees and 62 degrees. 48 plus 62 equals 110, and 180 minus 110 equals 70. The third angle is 70 degrees.
steps: Add the two angles you know. 61 plus 26 equals 87.
All three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Take the total away from 180 degrees. The third angle is 93 degrees. 180 minus 87 equals 93.

Q_CH19_007.q: One acute angle of a right-angled triangle measures 27 degrees. What is the other acute angle?
hints: This is a missing-angle problem in a right-angled triangle. One angle is 90 degrees, and the three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Since one angle is 90 degrees, the two acute angles share the other 90 degrees between them. Take the acute angle you know away from 90 degrees.

Here is a similar problem. One acute angle of a right-angled triangle is 35 degrees. The two acute angles add up to 90 degrees, so the other is 90 minus 35, which is 55 degrees. Check: 90 plus 35 plus 55 equals 180.
steps: A right-angled triangle has one angle of 90 degrees. The three angles add up to 180 degrees, so the two acute angles together make 180 minus 90, which is 90 degrees.
One acute angle is 27 degrees, so the other is 90 minus 27, which is 63.
So the other acute angle is 63 degrees.

Q_CH19_007_V04.q: Two angles of a triangle are 52 degrees and 73 degrees. What is the third angle?
hints: The three angles of a triangle always add up to 180 degrees. Two are given, so find what is left for the third.
First add the two angles you know, 52 degrees and 73 degrees. Then think about how far that total is from 180 degrees.
Similar example: two angles of a triangle are 33 degrees and 57 degrees. 33 plus 57 equals 90, and 180 minus 90 equals 90. The third angle is 90 degrees.
steps: Add the two angles you know. 52 plus 73 equals 125.
All three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
Take the total away from 180 degrees. The third angle is 55 degrees. 180 minus 125 equals 55.

Q_CH19_008.q: In a right-angled isosceles triangle, each of the equal angles measures:
hints: This triangle is both right-angled and isosceles. So one angle is 90 degrees and the other two angles are equal.
The three angles add up to 180 degrees. First take away the right angle to find what the two equal angles share.

Here is a similar problem. An isosceles triangle has one angle of 110 degrees and two equal angles. The two equal angles share 180 minus 110, which is 70 degrees, so each one is 70 divided by 2, which is 35 degrees.
steps: One angle is 90 degrees. The three angles add up to 180 degrees, so the other two together make 180 minus 90, which is 90 degrees.
The other two angles are equal, so each is half of 90 degrees. 90 divided by 2 equals 45.
So each of the equal angles measures 45 degrees.

Q_CH19_008_V04.q: What is the complement of an angle of 6 degrees?
hints: This is about complementary angles. Two angles are complementary when together they make a right angle.
Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. So take 6 degrees away from 90 degrees.
Similar example: the complement of 20 degrees is 90 degrees minus 20 degrees, which is 70 degrees. Check: 20 degrees plus 70 degrees equals 90 degrees.
steps: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 90 degrees. 90 degrees minus 6 degrees equals 84 degrees.
Check by adding: 6 degrees plus 84 degrees equals 90 degrees. The complement of 6 degrees is 84 degrees.

Q_CH19_009.q: Which of the following is not a type of triangle?
hints: Can you have a right angle and all sides equal?
Equilateral means all angles are 60 degrees. But right-angled means one angle is 90 degrees. Can one angle be both 60 degrees and 90 degrees?
No! A right-angled equilateral triangle is impossible.
steps: Equilateral: all angles are 60 degrees. Right-angled: one angle is 90 degrees. 60 degrees is not equal to 90 degrees.
These two properties contradict each other. It is impossible!
B is not a valid triangle type.

Q_CH19_010.q: Which of the following are the angles of an obtuse-angled scalene triangle?
hints: Two things must both be true here. Obtuse-angled means one angle is more than 90 degrees, and scalene means all three angles are different.
First set aside any set that has no angle bigger than 90 degrees. Then, in the sets that are left, see whether all three angles are different.

Here is a similar problem. Which is an acute-angled isosceles triangle: 70 degrees, 70 degrees, 40 degrees or 100 degrees, 40 degrees, 40 degrees? Both have two equal angles, so both are isosceles. Only in the first are all the angles less than 90 degrees, so 70 degrees, 70 degrees, 40 degrees is the acute-angled isosceles triangle.
steps: An obtuse-angled triangle has one angle more than 90 degrees. A scalene triangle has three different angles.
The sets 30 degrees, 60 degrees, 90 degrees and 50 degrees, 90 degrees, 40 degrees each have a largest angle of exactly 90 degrees, so they are right-angled, not obtuse-angled.
The set 150 degrees, 15 degrees, 15 degrees has an obtuse angle, but two of its angles are equal, so it is isosceles, not scalene.
In the last set, 120 degrees is more than 90 degrees and all three angles are different. So the obtuse-angled scalene triangle is 40 degrees, 120 degrees, 20 degrees.

Q_CH19_011.q: In a triangle, two interior angles are 55 degrees and 70 degrees. What is the exterior angle adjacent to the third angle?
hints: This is about an exterior angle of a triangle. An exterior angle and the interior angle next to it lie on a straight line, so together they make 180 degrees.
First find the third interior angle. The three interior angles add up to 180 degrees, so take 55 degrees and 70 degrees away from 180 degrees.

Here is a similar problem. Two interior angles of a triangle are 40 degrees and 60 degrees. The third interior angle is 180 minus 40 minus 60, which is 80 degrees. The exterior angle next to it is 180 minus 80, which is 100 degrees. Notice that this is the same as 40 plus 60.
steps: The three interior angles add up to 180 degrees, so the third interior angle is 180 minus 55 minus 70, which is 55 degrees.
The exterior angle and the third interior angle lie on a straight line, so together they make 180 degrees.
180 minus 55 equals 125, which is the same as 55 plus 70. So the exterior angle is 125 degrees.

Q_CH19_011_V03.q: What is the complement of an angle of 84 degrees?
hints: This is about complementary angles. Two angles are complementary when together they make a right angle.
Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees. So take 84 degrees away from 90 degrees.
Similar example: the complement of 20 degrees is 90 degrees minus 20 degrees, which is 70 degrees. Check: 20 degrees plus 70 degrees equals 90 degrees.
steps: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 90 degrees. 90 degrees minus 84 degrees equals 6 degrees.
Check by adding: 84 degrees plus 6 degrees equals 90 degrees. The complement of 84 degrees is 6 degrees.

Q_CH19_012.q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 130 degrees. One of the opposite interior angles is 50 degrees. What is the other?
hints: This uses a fact about triangles: an exterior angle is equal to the sum of the two interior angles opposite it, the ones that are not next to it.
The two opposite interior angles add up to 130 degrees. One of them is 50 degrees, so think about what must be added to 50 degrees to make 130 degrees.

Here is a similar problem. An exterior angle of a triangle is 110 degrees, and one of the opposite interior angles is 45 degrees. The two opposite interior angles add up to 110 degrees, so the other is 110 minus 45, which is 65 degrees.
steps: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles. So those two angles add up to 130 degrees.
One of them is 50 degrees, so the other is 130 minus 50, which is 80.
Check: the interior angle beside the exterior angle is 180 minus 130, which is 50 degrees, and 50 plus 50 plus 80, which is 180. So the other angle is 80 degrees.

Q_CH19_012_V04.q: What is the supplement of an angle of 12 degrees?
hints: This is about supplementary angles. Two angles are supplementary when together they make a straight line.
Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees. So take 12 degrees away from 180 degrees.
Similar example: the supplement of 70 degrees is 180 degrees minus 70 degrees, which is 110 degrees. Check: 70 degrees plus 110 degrees equals 180 degrees.
steps: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees.
Take the given angle away from 180 degrees. 180 degrees minus 12 degrees equals 168 degrees.
Check by adding: 12 degrees plus 168 degrees equals 180 degrees. The supplement of 12 degrees is 168 degrees.

Q_CH19_013.q: In an isosceles triangle, each base angle is 70 degrees. What is the vertex angle?
hints: This is a missing-angle problem. An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles and one vertex angle, and the three angles add up to 180 degrees.
Both base angles are 70 degrees. First add the two base angles together.
Here is a similar problem. Each base angle of an isosceles triangle is 65 degrees. The two base angles make 65 plus 65, which is 130 degrees. The vertex angle is 180 minus 130, which is 50 degrees.
steps: The two base angles are 70 degrees each, so together they make 70 plus 70, which is 140 degrees.
The three angles add up to 180 degrees, so the vertex angle is 180 minus 140, which is 40.
So the vertex angle is 40 degrees.

Q_CH19_013_V04.q: Two angles of a triangle are 75 degrees and 74 degrees. What is the third angle?
